clinical_profile.unified_indications: Relief of flatulence, abdominal discomfort, and infant colic due to entrapped gas. Also indicated for symptoms associated with Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS).
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: N/A
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Dry mouth, thirst, and dizziness (feeling of being sleepy).
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Caution is advised for patients with actual or suspected glaucoma (eye conditions that damage the optic nerve) or prostatic hypertrophy (increase in volume of prostate gland). This medication may exacerbate acid reflux in patients with hiatus hernia. Patients should avoid driving or operating heavy machinery due to the potential for dizziness. Concurrent consumption of alcohol should be avoided. The effect of this medicine is undetermined in lactating females; consultation with a healthcare provider is recommended before use during lactation.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Contraindicated in pregnant females.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Specific dosage guidelines are not provided in the available data. Clinical dosage should be determined by a healthcare professional based on patient-specific factors and full product labeling.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Treatment of bacterial and fungal skin diseases.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Chorquinaldol acts as an antimicrobial agent effective against fungal and bacterial infections.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: No specific side effects, such as burning or itching on wounds, are reported in the available data.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: No specific general warnings or precautions are reported in the available data.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Contraindicated during pregnancy and lactation.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Available as ointment and cream formulations. Available over-the-counter (OTC) without a prescription.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Steroidal cream indicated for fungal infections (mycotic fungal infections) and gram-positive bacterial infections.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Diflucortolone is a potent corticosteroid, providing anti-inflammatory, anti-allergic, and antipruritic effects. Isoconazole is an azole antifungal that inhibits ergosterol synthesis, essential for fungal cell membrane integrity, leading to fungal cell death.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Increased risk of opportunistic infections (rare), endocrine disorders, weight changes, osteoporosis, increased blood sugar levels, skin atrophy, stretch marks, thinning or wrinkling of skin, increased or decreased skin pigmentation, hirsutism. Long-term use around the eyes may lead to glaucoma.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: For external use only. Avoid use if allergic to isoconazole nitrate, diflucortolone valerate, or any other ingredients. Skin lesions due to systemic tuberculosis, syphilis, or other diseases must be treated appropriately to eliminate the primary cause. Use cautiously in patients with severe kidney or liver disease. Additional medicines may be needed for severe fungal infections. Patients with endocrine syndromes or disorders should consult a doctor. Use only if necessary and avoid long periods unless advised by a doctor. Share relevant medical history and pre-existing conditions. Not recommended for pregnant females, especially in the first trimester; consult a doctor. Use in nursing females only if necessary; consult a doctor. Dose adjustment may be needed in children or the elderly due to absorption rate differences. Long-term use around the eyes may lead to glaucoma. Avoid use on the face unless absolutely necessary due to risk of skin thinning or wrinkling. Avoid use near the eyes. While not known to affect contraception, it is contraindicated in pregnancy; discuss alternatives if planning pregnancy.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Severe endocrine disorders, history of allergic reactions to steroids or any ingredients in the medicine. Pregnancy.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Apply consistently. Improvement typically observed within 3-4 days, with full benefits usually seen in about 2 weeks. Treatment should ideally not exceed 2 weeks unless advised by a doctor. If symptoms do not improve or worsen, consult a doctor. Prescription is ideally needed. A dose adjustment may be necessary for children or the elderly due to differences in absorption rates.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Indicated for all dermatoses responsive to topical corticosteroid therapy, including eczema. Not suitable for peri-oral dermatitis (facial rash) and rosacea (visible blood vessels in your face; redness).
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: As a topical corticosteroid, diflucortolone valerate exerts anti-inflammatory, immunosuppressive, and vasoconstrictive effects.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Patients may experience burning, itching, irritation, erythema (redness), dryness, thinning of the skin, telangiectasia (dilation of blood vessels close to the surface), striae (formation of stripes on skin), hypertrichosis (increased body hair growth), perioral dermatitis (a facial rash that tends to occur around the mouth), and various other skin reactions. If any of these symptoms persist for a long period, consult your doctor immediately.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: This medicine should be used with extreme caution, especially when taken in high doses, as systemic effects can result from the use of more potent steroids. If local irritation occurs, discontinue use. Skin atrophy may become clinically significant after prolonged use. Do not use this steroid as sole therapy, and avoid prolonged use (limit to 7 days). There is a risk of visual disturbances. Elderly patients must be cautious. For pregnant females, this medicine should only be used when clearly needed, and consultation with a doctor is advised. For nursing females, the effects are undetermined; consult a doctor. Apply a thin layer only. May cause adverse effects if combined with Vitamin C. Inform your doctor if symptoms do not improve within a week.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Contraindicated in patients with areas of tuberculous or syphilitic processes, and for the treatment of viral diseases such as vaccinia (smallpox), chickenpox, and shingles (herpes zoster). Not recommended for use in pregnant or nursing females; for pregnancy, it should only be used when clearly needed after physician consultation. For nursing females, effects are undetermined, and consultation with a doctor is advised.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Wash hands before and after application. Apply a thin layer of the medicine evenly to the affected area. Avoid prolonged use, generally limiting application to 7 days.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Treatment of exocrine pancreatic insufficiency associated with conditions such as cystic fibrosis, chronic pancreatitis, or pancreatectomy. Also used for disturbances of protein and carbohydrate digestion, digestive stress, dyspepsia (indigestion), over-eating, imbalanced diet after post-meal distress, abdominal distention, belching, heart-burn, diarrhea in old age and children, loss of appetite, loss of taste, and food intolerance.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Pancreatic enzyme products contain a mixture of lipases, proteases, and amylases that catalyze the hydrolysis of fats to monoglyceride, glycerol and free fatty acids, proteins into peptides and amino acids, and starches into dextrins and short chain sugars such as maltose and maltriose in the duodenum and proximal small intestine, thereby acting like digestive enzymes physiologically secreted by the pancreas.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Patients may experience slight discomfort and gas. Other common adverse reactions reported include vomiting, dizziness, cough, irritability, decreased appetite, hyperglycemia, hypoglycemia, abdominal pain, abnormal feces, flatulence, frequent bowel movements, and nasopharyngitis.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Serious warnings include Fibrosing Colonopathy, Irritation of the Oral Mucosa, Hyperuricemia, Risk of Viral Transmission, and Hypersensitivity Reactions. Pregnant and lactating females should consult a doctor before use as the effects of this medicine are unknown in these populations. Patients with liver or kidney impairment or any other severe disorders/diseases should use this medicine cautiously.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: None.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Dosing is based on lipase units and should be individualized based on clinical symptoms, the degree of steatorrhea present, and the fat content of the diet. Do not exceed 2,500 lipase units/kg/meal, 10,000 lipase units/kg/day, or 4,000 lipase units/g fat ingested/day in adult and pediatric patients greater than 12 months of age without further investigation. The total daily dosage in adult and pediatric patients greater than 12 months of age should reflect approximately three meals plus two or three snacks per day. With each snack, administer approximately half the prescribed dose for a meal. Do not substitute other pancreatic enzyme products for specific formulations like CREON. When switching from another pancreatic enzyme product, monitor patients for clinical symptoms of exocrine pancreatic insufficiency.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Treatment of irregular heart rhythms and heart diseases such as congestive heart failure.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Digoxin inhibits sodium-potassium ATPase, an enzyme that regulates the quantity of sodium and potassium inside cells. Inhibition of the enzyme leads to an increase in the intracellular concentration of sodium and thus (by stimulation of sodium-calcium exchange) an increase in the intracellular concentration of calcium. The beneficial effects of digoxin result from direct actions on cardiac muscle, as well as indirect actions on the cardiovascular system mediated by effects on the autonomic nervous system. The autonomic effects include: (1) a vagomimetic action, which is responsible for the effects of digoxin on the sinoatrial and atrioventricular (AV) nodes; and (2) baroreceptor sensitization, which results in increased afferent inhibitory activity and reduced activity of the sympathetic nervous system and renin-angiotensin system for any given increment in mean arterial pressure. clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Adverse reactions to digoxin are generally dose-dependent and occur more frequently at doses higher than those needed for therapeutic effect, or in susceptible patients. These can include: anorexia (loss of appetite), nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, visual disturbances, headache, fatigue, drowsiness, confusion, delirium, hallucinations, depression, cardiac arrhythmias, and heartblock. Rarely reported side effects include rash, intestinal ischemia (painful intestines), gynecomastia (enlargement of men's breasts) on long-term use, and thrombocytopenia (deficiency of platelets). Cardiac, gastrointestinal, and CNS disturbances account for the majority of adverse reactions.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Caution is advised due to individual patient sensitivity, associated conditions, and concurrent medications. Dosage must be carefully selected and adjusted. Specific precautions include: recent myocardial infarction, sick sinus syndrome, thyroid disease, and the need to avoid hypokalemia (deficiency of potassium in blood). Reduce dose in elderly patients and those with kidney impairment. Rapid intravenous administration should be avoided due to the risk of nausea and arrhythmias. Pregnancy: Effects are undetermined; caution is advised, and healthcare provider consultation is necessary. Lactation: Caution advised or effect undetermined; consult your healthcare provider for further guidance. Alcohol: Avoid consumption while taking this medicine. Dosage selection must consider the patient's lean body weight, renal function (estimated creatinine clearance), age (different doses for infants, children, and elderly, with advanced age often indicating diminished renal function), and any concomitant disease states or medications that may alter digoxin's pharmacokinetic or pharmacodynamic profile.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Digitalis glycosides are contraindicated in patients with ventricular fibrillation or in patients with a known hypersensitivity to digoxin. A hypersensitivity reaction to other digitalis preparations usually constitutes a contraindication to digoxin.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Dosage of digoxin requires considerable modification based on individual patient sensitivity, associated conditions, and concurrent medications. Doses should be calculated based on lean (ideal) body weight, renal function (preferably estimated creatinine clearance), and age (infants, children, and elderly patients require different considerations, with advanced age often indicating diminished renal function even with normal serum creatinine). Concomitant disease states and concurrent medications that may alter digoxin's pharmacokinetic or pharmacodynamic profile must also be considered. Serum digoxin concentrations should generally guide dose determination. Reduction in dosage is necessary for elderly patients and those with kidney impairment.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Prevention and treatment of malaria.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: N/A
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Abdominal pain, anorexia, diarrhea, vomiting, nausea, palpitation, and dizziness.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Patients should be careful about electrolyte disturbances and concurrent use with drugs that might cause heartbeat irregularities (QT-interval prolongation). Patients who cannot take food should be monitored. Avoid alcohol consumption.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Pregnancy, lactation, history of arrhythmia or bradycardia, and congestive heart failure with reduced ventricular ejection.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Treatment of amoebiasis (including intestinal and other systemic forms caused by E. histolytica) and giardiasis. Also used for other infections caused by susceptible bacteria and parasites, given metronidazole's broad-spectrum activity.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Diloxanide furoate is a luminal amoebicide, acting directly on the trophozoites of E. histolytica in the intestinal lumen. Metronidazole is a nitroimidazole antimicrobial that, once intracellularly reduced, forms reactive cytotoxic compounds that disrupt DNA and protein synthesis, leading to cell death of susceptible anaerobic bacteria and protozoa.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Gastrointestinal distress (e.g., upset stomach). Other potential adverse effects include agitation, blurred vision, tingling sensation, confusion, dizziness, and headache. (Note: Metronidazole can also cause metallic taste, nausea, and neuropathies).
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Patients should be advised to take this medicine exactly as prescribed by their doctor and to complete the entire course of treatment to prevent recurrence of infection, even if symptoms improve. Do not exceed the recommended daily dose. Dosage should not be altered without medical approval. If the medicine does not suit the patient, discontinue use immediately. Long-term use requires physician approval. Consult a doctor before using other antibiotics concurrently. Avoid consuming alcohol and marijuana during treatment due to potential disulfiram-like reactions (with metronidazole) and exacerbation of side effects like dizziness. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery as this medicine may impair ability. This medicine may reduce the effectiveness of condoms; discuss alternative contraceptives with a doctor. Store at room temperature away from direct heat and sunlight, and out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiry date or if the quality seal is broken or missing. Inform your doctor about your complete medical history before starting this medication.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Known hypersensitivity or allergy to diloxanide, metronidazole, or any other constituents of the formulation. Not recommended for use during pregnancy or lactation due to potential risks.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Dosage and duration of treatment must be strictly as advised by a healthcare professional. It is imperative to complete the full course of therapy, as premature discontinuation can lead to treatment failure or recurrence of infection. Do not stop taking the medicine even if symptoms improve before the prescribed course is finished. Do not exceed the recommended daily dose or alter the dosage regimen without consulting a physician.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Treatment of amoebiasis (amoebic infections), including amoebic dysentery and asymptomatic cyst passers, giardiasis (infection of the small intestine), and other systemic diseases caused by E. histolytica organisms. Additionally, indicated for stomach infections, various skin and mouth infections, rosacea, bacterial vaginosis, and pelvic inflammatory disease, primarily attributed to the metronidazole component.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: The specific mechanism of action for diloxanide furoate is not explicitly detailed. Metronidazole functions as an antimicrobial agent, effective against a wide range of anaerobic bacteria and protozoa.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Commonly reported side effects include abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, and general gastrointestinal distress. The medication may also cause blurred vision, and patients may experience tingling or pain in the hands or feet.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Complete the full prescribed course of treatment, even if symptoms improve. Store at room temperature below 30°C, away from sources of heat and direct light. Do not chew or crush tablets; swallow them whole. Inform your doctor about your complete medical history, including any conditions like alcohol intoxication, liver disease, excessive alcohol consumption, lower seizure threshold, or a history of seizures, and any tingling or pain in the hands or feet. Use with extreme caution in patients with neurodegenerative disorders of the brain (e.g., multiple sclerosis), epilepsy, or other convulsive disorders. Due to potential blurred vision or dizziness, avoid driving or performing high-alert activities until you know how this medicine affects you. Caution is advised in patients with liver or kidney disease, as the safety and effectiveness in these populations are undetermined. Inform your doctor about all current medications, especially anticoagulants, ciclosporin, other antimicrobials, cimetidine, fluorouracil, phenytoin, lithium, or phenobarbital, as interactions may occur. Do not discontinue this medication without consulting your doctor. Do not share this medicine with others. While generally contraindicated in pregnancy and lactation, consult a doctor for a case-specific risk/benefit analysis if use is deemed absolutely necessary.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Management of angina (chest pain) and hypertension (high blood pressure). Also used for heart rate reduction in conditions like atrial fibrillation/flutter or PSVT.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Diltiazem is a non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker. It inhibits the influx of extracellular calcium ions across the myocardial and vascular smooth muscle cell membranes, leading to coronary and peripheral vasodilation, reduction in myocardial contractility, and slowing of AV nodal conduction.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common adverse events reported during clinical trials include hypotension (asymptomatic 4.3%, symptomatic 3.2%), injection site reactions (e.g., itching, burning, 3.9%), vasodilation/flushing (1.7%), and arrhythmia (junctional rhythm or isorhythmic dissociation, 1%). clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Diltiazem is not recommended for pregnant or nursing females. It might cause dizziness or tiredness; patients should avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until they know how this medicine affects them. Use with caution in patients with liver disease or kidney disease. Avoid alcohol consumption while using this medicine. Before using, inform your doctor about your complete medical history, especially if you have heart, liver, or kidney diseases, depression, or gut problems. Inform your doctor about all your current medicines and if you are about to undergo surgery. Do not quit this medicine without informing your doctor. Do not share this medicine with anyone. Caution is advised in patients with sick sinus syndrome or AV block without a functioning ventricular pacemaker.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Hypersensitivity to the drug. Contraindicated in patients with sick sinus syndrome (unless a functioning ventricular pacemaker is present), second- or third-degree AV block (unless a functioning ventricular pacemaker is present), severe hypotension, or cardiogenic shock. Intravenous diltiazem and intravenous beta-blockers should not be administered together or in close proximity (within a few hours). Contraindicated in patients with atrial fibrillation or atrial flutter associated with an accessory bypass tract (e.g., Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome or short PR syndrome).
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: For direct intravenous single injections (Bolus): The initial dose is 0.25 mg/kg actual body weight (e.g., 20 mg for an average patient) administered over 2 minutes. If the response is inadequate, a second dose of 0.35 mg/kg actual body weight (e.g., 25 mg for an average patient) may be administered after 15 minutes over 2 minutes. Subsequent intravenous bolus doses should be individualized. Patients with low body weights should be dosed on a mg/kg basis. Some patients may respond to an initial dose of 0.15 mg/kg, although experience with this dose is limited and duration of action may be shorter. Continuous intravenous infusion is also used for continued reduction of heart rate (up to 24 hours) in patients with atrial fibrillation or atrial flutter.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Induction of labor, including cervical ripening.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Dinoprostone functions as a local hormone, secreted by fetal membranes and placenta, playing a key role in the initiation of labor and cervical ripening. It stimulates the production of prostaglandin F2α (PGF2α), which sensitizes the myometrium to endogenous or exogenously administered oxytocin, leading to cervical changes (tissue consistency, dilatation, and effacement) and potentially systemic effects such as uterine tachysystole or hypersystole/hypertonicity.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common adverse reactions include uterine hypercontractility/tachysystole (with or without fetal distress) and fetal distress. Severe adverse reactions reported include Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC) and Amniotic Fluid Embolism.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Extreme caution is advised in patients with cardiovascular, hepatic, and renal dysfunction. Careful monitoring for Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC), Amniotic Fluid Embolism, uterine tachysystole, and uterine hypersystole/hypertonicity is essential. Continuous monitoring of uterine activity, fetal status, and the progression of cervical dilatation and effacement is required. Dinoprostone should only be administered by trained obstetrical personnel in a hospital setting with appropriate obstetrical care facilities. Consult a doctor before using in pregnancy (risk cannot be ruled out) and during lactation. Avoid driving as it may affect the ability to drive.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to prostaglandins; evidence or clinical suspicion of fetal distress where delivery is not imminent; unexplained vaginal bleeding in the current pregnancy; evidence or clinical suspicion of marked cephalopelvic disproportion; conditions for which induction of labor or oxytocic drugs are contraindicated; previous cesarean section or other uterine surgery expected to affect uterine integrity (e.g., myomectomy); conditions under which prolonged contraction of the uterus may be detrimental to fetal safety; concurrent use with intravenous oxytocic agents; and six or more previous term pregnancies.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Administer a single vaginal insert (10 mg) intravaginally for up to 12 hours (releasing approximately 0.3 mg of dinoprostone per hour). Remove the insert upon onset of active labor or after 12 hours. Continuous monitoring of uterine activity, fetal status, and cervical progression is crucial. Administration must be performed by trained obstetrical personnel in a hospital setting with appropriate obstetrical care facilities.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Divalproex sodium is indicated for the treatment of various forms of epilepsy and seizures, including complex partial seizures. It is also used for mania. clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Divalproex sodium dissociates to the valproate ion in the gastrointestinal tract. clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Patients may experience gastrointestinal upset, weight gain, hair loss, headache, liver injury, rash, aggression, bone marrow failure, easy bruising/bleeding, sore throat, nausea/vomiting, yellowing eyes/skin, stomach/abdominal pain, constipation, dark urine, unusual tiredness/weakness, signs of infection, and unusual/sudden weight gain. Serious adverse reactions include hepatic failure, birth defects, decreased IQ following in utero exposure, pancreatitis, hyperammonemic encephalopathy, suicidal behavior and ideation, bleeding and other hematopoietic disorders, hypothermia, Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS)/Multiorgan hypersensitivity reactions, and somnolence in the elderly. If any of these symptoms are persistent or severe, consult a doctor immediately.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Pregnant ladies must consult their doctor before taking this medicine for a better analysis, as divalproex sodium can cause birth defects and decreased IQ following in utero exposure. Patients who are allergic to divalproex sodium or any of its components should consult a doctor before use. Caution is advised if taking any vitamins, nutritional supplements, or herbal products. If swelling is experienced, consult a doctor immediately. High concentrations of divalproex sodium might result in severe pain. Patients should be monitored for hepatic failure, especially during the first six months of treatment, which may be preceded by non-specific symptoms such as malaise, weakness, lethargy, facial edema, anorexia, and vomiting. Pancreatitis, hyperammonemic encephalopathy, suicidal behavior and ideation, bleeding and other hematopoietic disorders, hypothermia, and DRESS/multiorgan hypersensitivity reactions are serious risks. Somnolence may occur in the elderly. Driving should be avoided when taking this medicine as it may affect ability to drive. Alcohol consumption should be avoided. If a patient has had a false positive urine test for diabetes or is a woman of child-bearing age, they should consult their doctor before using this medication.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Divalproex sodium is contraindicated in patients with hepatic disease or significant hepatic dysfunction. clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Divalproex sodium extended-release tablets are intended for once-a-day oral administration. They should be taken by mouth with food, as directed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet whole; do not crush or chew it, as this can irritate the mouth or throat. Do not increase the quantity or take this product more often than directed. For mania, the initial dose is 25 mg/kg/day, increasing as rapidly as possible to achieve therapeutic response or desired plasma level, with a maximum recommended dosage of 60 mg/kg/day. For complex partial seizures, start at 10 mg/kg/day to 15 mg/kg/day, increasing at 1-week intervals by 5 mg/kg/day to 10 mg/kg/day to achieve optimal clinical response, with a maximum recommended dosage of 60 mg/kg/day. If response is not satisfactory, check valproate plasma levels. Store at room temperature and keep out of reach of children.

clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: The most serious adverse reactions associated with docetaxel include toxic deaths, hepatic impairment, hematologic effects (such as neutropenia), enterocolitis and neutropenic colitis, severe hypersensitivity reactions (including anaphylaxis), fluid retention, second primary malignancies, cutaneous reactions, neurologic reactions, eye disorders, asthenia, and tumor lysis syndrome. Common adverse reactions across all indications include infection.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Docetaxel carries warnings regarding: increased treatment-related mortality (toxic deaths), particularly in patients with abnormal liver function, higher doses, or NSCLC patients with prior platinum-based chemotherapy at 100 mg/m²; significant hepatic impairment; severe hematologic effects, notably neutropenia (requiring baseline neutrophil counts); enterocolitis and neutropenic colitis; potentially life-threatening hypersensitivity reactions; severe fluid retention; the risk of second primary malignancies; various cutaneous reactions; neurologic toxicities; eye disorders; asthenia; and tumor lysis syndrome. The alcohol content in certain formulations may also be a consideration. Administration should occur in a facility prepared to manage acute complications.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Docetaxel is contraindicated in patients with neutrophil counts of <1500 cells/mm³ and those with a history of severe hypersensitivity reactions to docetaxel, including anaphylaxis.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines:
Administer docetaxel intravenously over 1 hour every 3 weeks in a facility equipped to manage possible complications (e.g., anaphylaxis). Do not substitute BEIZRAY for other docetaxel products. 
*   **Locally Advanced or Metastatic Breast Cancer**: 60 mg/m² to 100 mg/m² as a single agent. 
*   **Adjuvant Breast Cancer**: 75 mg/m² administered 1 hour after doxorubicin 50 mg/m² and cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m² every 3 weeks for 6 cycles. 
*   **Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC)**: After platinum therapy failure: 75 mg/m² as a single agent. Chemotherapy-naive: 75 mg/m² followed by cisplatin 75 mg/m². 
*   **Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer (CRPC)**: 75 mg/m² with 5 mg prednisone twice a day continuously. 
*   **Gastric Carcinoma (GC)**: 75 mg/m² followed by cisplatin 75 mg/m² (both on day 1 only) followed by fluorouracil 750 mg/m² per day as a 24-hour IV (days 1-5), starting at the end of cisplatin infusion. 
*   **Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck (SCCHN)**: 75 mg/m² followed by cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV (day 1), followed by fluorouracil 750 mg/m² per day as a 24-hour IV (days 1-5), starting at the end of cisplatin infusion.
clinical_profile.black_box_warning: WARNING: TOXIC DEATHS, HEPATOTOXICITY, NEUTROPENIA, HYPERSENSITIVITY REACTIONS, and FLUID RETENTION. Treatment-related mortality associated with docetaxel is increased in patients with abnormal liver function, in patients receiving higher doses, and in patients with non-small cell lung carcinoma and a history of prior treatment with platinum-based chemotherapy who receive docetaxel as a single agent at a dose of 100 mg/m². Avoid the use of docetaxel in patients with abnormal liver function.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Treatment of elevated intraocular pressure in patients with ocular hypertension and open-angle glaucoma, either as monotherapy or as an adjunct to beta-blockers, particularly in patients unresponsive to beta-blockers or when beta-blockers are contraindicated.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Dorzolamide hydrochloride is an inhibitor of human carbonic anhydrase II (CA-II). CA-II is found in various tissues, including the eye. Inhibition of carbonic anhydrase in the ciliary processes of the eye decreases aqueous humor secretion, presumably by slowing the formation of bicarbonate ions with subsequent reduction in sodium and fluid transport, leading to a reduction in intraocular pressure (IOP). Following topical ocular administration, dorzolamide reduces elevated intraocular pressure.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Ocular burning, stinging, or discomfort immediately following administration (common, approximately one-third of patients); bitter taste (common, approximately one-quarter of patients); superficial punctate keratitis (10-15% of patients); signs and symptoms of ocular allergic reaction (approximately 10% of patients); itching, blurred vision, conjunctivitis, nausea, fatigue, and tearing.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Pregnancy: Pregnant females should consult their doctors before using this medicine. Lactation: Lactating females should consult their doctors before using this medicine. Hepatic/Liver Impairment: Caution is advised, and consultation with a doctor is recommended for patients with hepatic impairment. Renal/Kidney Impairment: Caution is advised, and consultation with a doctor is recommended for patients with kidney impairment or a history of renal calculi. Alcohol: Alcohol is prohibited while using this medicine. Driving: While generally considered safe to drive sometime after use, caution is advised, especially if experiencing blurred vision or other ocular side effects. Additional precautions include use with care in patients with chronic corneal defects, a history of intraocular surgery, closed-angle glaucoma, or sulphonamide hypersensitivity.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Dorzolamide hydrochloride ophthalmic solution is contraindicated in patients who are hypersensitive to any component of this product, including those with known sulphonamide hypersensitivity.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Administer one drop of dorzolamide hydrochloride ophthalmic solution into the affected eye(s) three times daily. If used concomitantly with other topical ophthalmic medications, a minimum interval of five minutes should be observed between administrations.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: This medication is indicated for the reduction of elevated intraocular pressure in patients with open-angle glaucoma.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Dorzolamide is a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor that reduces aqueous humor secretion by inhibiting the enzyme carbonic anhydrase II in the ciliary body. Timolol is a non-selective beta-adrenergic receptor blocker that reduces aqueous humor production. The combined action of these two components leads to a synergistic reduction in intraocular pressure.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common side effects include ocular irritation, blurred vision, headache, nausea, fatigue, and corneal erosion. Systemic effects may also occur.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Precautions should be exercised in patients with hypotension (low blood pressure), uncontrolled heart failure, a history of severe cardiac (heart) disease, hepatic (liver) impairment, diabetes mellitus, hyperthyroidism (excessive activity of the thyroid gland), and mild to moderate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Doxazosin is indicated for the treatment of hypertension (high blood pressure) and benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), including symptoms associated with prostatic enlargement and urinary outflow obstruction.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common side effects include postural effects, dizziness, vertigo (fainting), asthenia (physical weakness/fatigue), edema (fluid retention in body), nausea, rhinitis (swelling of mucosal membrane of nose), somnolence (sleepiness), palpitation, tachycardia (high heart rate), anxiety, insomnia (inability to sleep), nervousness, paresthesia (abnormal sensation of skin), hypotension (low blood pressure), cough, dyspnoea (difficulty in breathing), GI upset, anorexia (loss of appetite for food), dry mouth, pruritus (unpleasant sensation of skin), back pain, urinary tract infection (UTI), influenza-like symptoms, chest pain, and headache. Dizziness, fatigue, hypotension, edema, and dyspnoea have been noted to have a significantly higher incidence than placebo, with dizziness and dyspnoea appearing to be dose-related.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Risk of priapism (prolonged erection); seek immediate medical assistance if it occurs. Monitor blood pressure regularly, especially 2 to 6 hours after the first dose and with each increase in dose, due to the risk of postural hypotension and first-dose syncope. Concomitant administration of doxazosin with a PDE-5 inhibitor can result in additive blood pressure lowering effects and symptomatic hypotension; therefore, PDE-5 inhibitor therapy should be initiated at the lowest dose in patients taking doxazosin. Doxazosin is contraindicated in lactating females. Pregnancy: No definite data regarding pregnancy is available; therefore, use with caution and consult a doctor. Avoid driving and operating machinery as doxazosin may affect the ability to drive. Avoid consuming alcohol while taking this medicine. Use with caution in patients with pulmonary edema, high output cardiac failure, right-sided heart failure due to pulmonary embolism, left ventricular heart failure, and liver impairment. Caution is advised during cataract surgery due to the risk of Intraoperative Floppy Iris Syndrome (IFIS).
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Doxazosin is contraindicated in patients with a known sensitivity to quinazolines (e.g., prazosin, terazosin), doxazosin, or any of the inert ingredients. It is also contraindicated in lactating females.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Dosage must be individualized. The initial dosage of doxazosin for hypertension and/or benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is 1 mg given orally once daily, either in the morning or evening. This starting dose is intended to minimize the frequency of postural hypotension and first-dose syncope. If doxazosin administration is discontinued for several days, therapy should be restarted using the initial 1 mg daily dosing regimen. For BPH, the dosage typically ranges from 1 to 8 mg once daily.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Treatment of hypertension (high blood pressure) and benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), including symptoms associated with urinary outflow obstruction and prostate enlargement.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Doxazosin selectively blocks alpha 1-adrenergic receptors. In benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), this blockade decreases urethral resistance and relieves symptoms by relaxing smooth muscle in the prostate and bladder neck. For hypertension, it causes vasodilation by blocking alpha 1-adrenergic receptors in the peripheral vasculature, leading to a reduction in blood pressure.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Dizziness, postural effects, vertigo (fainting), asthenia (physical weakness/malaise), edema (fluid retention), nausea, rhinitis (swelling of nasal mucosal membrane), somnolence (sleepiness), palpitation, tachycardia (high heart rate), anxiety, insomnia (inability to sleep), nervousness, paresthesia (abnormal sensation of skin), hypotension (low blood pressure), cough, dyspnoea (difficulty in breathing), gastrointestinal upset, anorexia (loss of appetite), dry mouth, pruritus (unpleasant skin sensation), back pain, urinary tract infection (UTI), flu-like symptoms.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Patients, especially after the initial dose or dose increase, should be monitored for orthostatic hypotension and associated symptoms (e.g., dizziness, fainting). Blood pressure should be monitored for at least 6 hours following administration of the initial dose and each dose increase. No definite data regarding pregnancy is available; use with caution and only if clearly needed after consulting a doctor. Contraindicated in lactating females. Avoid driving or operating machinery due to potential for dizziness or somnolence, especially at the start of therapy or with dose increases. Avoid consuming alcohol due to potential to enhance hypotensive effects. Use with caution in patients with pulmonary edema, high output cardiac failure, right-sided heart failure due to pulmonary embolism, or left ventricular heart failure. Administer with caution in patients with impaired liver function. The use of alpha-1 blockers has been associated with Intraoperative Floppy Iris Syndrome (IFIS) during cataract surgery; patients should inform their ophthalmologist about doxazosin use. There is a risk of priapism (prolonged, painful erection); patients should be advised to seek immediate medical assistance if this occurs. If therapy is discontinued for several days, it should be restarted using the initial dosing regimen.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Hypersensitivity to doxazosin, other quinazolines (e.g., prazosin, terazosin), or any other component/ingredient of the product. Contraindicated in lactating females.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Administer once daily. Following the initial dose and with each dose increase, monitor blood pressure for at least 6 hours post-administration to assess for orthostatic effects. If therapy is discontinued for several days, restart with the initial dosing regimen. For Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH): Initiate therapy at 1 mg once daily. The dose may be titrated at 1 to 2-week intervals to 2 mg, then to 4 mg, and finally to 8 mg once daily, based on patient response and tolerability. The maximum recommended dose for BPH is 8 mg once daily. For Hypertension: Initiate therapy at 1 mg once daily. The dose may be titrated as needed, up to a maximum of 16 mg once daily.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Doxorubicin is indicated for the treatment of various cancers, including adjuvant breast cancer and other solid tumors, often used as a single agent or in combination with other chemotherapy drugs.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: The cytotoxic effect of doxorubicin hydrochloride on malignant cells and its toxic effects on various organs are primarily related to nucleotide base intercalation into DNA and cell membrane lipid binding activities. This intercalation inhibits nucleotide replication and the action of DNA and RNA polymerases. Additionally, the interaction of doxorubicin with topoisomerase II to form DNA-cleavable complexes is considered an important mechanism of its cytocidal activity.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: The most common adverse reactions (>10%) include alopecia, nausea, and vomiting. Other clinically significant adverse reactions can include cardiomyopathy and arrhythmias, secondary malignancies, extravasation and tissue necrosis, severe myelosuppression, tumor lysis syndrome, and radiation sensitization and recall.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Patients receiving doxorubicin are at risk for serious adverse events. These include cardiomyopathy (potentially leading to myocardial damage and acute left ventricular failure), secondary malignancies, extravasation with potential for tissue necrosis at the injection site, severe myelosuppression (which can be persistent), tumor lysis syndrome, and radiation sensitization or radiation recall phenomenon. Arrhythmias can also occur. The risk of cardiomyopathy is cumulative dose-dependent. Discontinuation of treatment is warranted if signs or symptoms of cardiomyopathy develop. Dose adjustments are required for patients with hepatic impairment.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Doxorubicin is contraindicated in patients with severe myocardial insufficiency, recent (within the past 4 to 6 weeks) myocardial infarction, severe persistent drug-induced myelosuppression, severe hepatic impairment (defined as Child Pugh Class C or serum bilirubin level greater than 5 mg/dL), or a history of severe hypersensitivity reaction to doxorubicin, including anaphylaxis.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: For single-agent therapy, the recommended dosage is 60 to 75 mg/m² administered intravenously every 21 days. In combination chemotherapy, the recommended dosage ranges from 40 to 75 mg/m² intravenously every 21 to 28 days. For adjuvant breast cancer, a recommended dosage is 60 mg/m² administered as an intravenous bolus on day 1 of each 21-day treatment cycle, in combination with cyclophosphamide, for a total of four cycles. Doxorubicin hydrochloride for injection should be discontinued in patients who develop signs or symptoms of cardiomyopathy. Dose reduction is necessary for patients with hepatic impairment.
clinical_profile.black_box_warning: WARNING: CARDIOMYOPATHY, SECONDARY MALIGNANCIES, EXTRAVASATION AND TISSUE NECROSIS, and SEVERE MYELOSUPPRESSION. Cardiomyopathy: Myocardial damage, including acute left ventricular failure, can occur with doxorubicin hydrochloride. The risk of cardiomyopathy is proportional to the cumulative exposure with incidence rates from 1% to 20% for cumulative doses ranging from 300 mg/m² to 500 mg/m² when doxorubicin hydrochloride is administered every 3 weeks. The risk of cardiomyopathy is further increased with pre-existing cardiac disease, prior or concomitant mediastinal radiation, or concomitant use of other cardiotoxic agents. Secondary Malignancies: Doxorubicin hydrochloride can increase the risk of developing secondary malignancies, including acute myeloid leukemia and myelodysplastic syndrome. Extravasation and Tissue Necrosis: Extravasation of doxorubicin hydrochloride can cause severe local tissue necrosis, which may require surgical intervention. Severe Myelosuppression: Doxorubicin hydrochloride can cause severe myelosuppression, including leukopenia, neutropenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia, leading to life-threatening infections and hemorrhage.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Doxycycline is indicated for the treatment of various bacterial infections, including respiratory tract infections, skin and soft tissue infections, and urinary tract infections.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Not available in provided data.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common side effects include gastrointestinal upset (anorexia, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, glossitis, dysphagia, enterocolitis, pancreatitis), inflammation of the esophagus, and esophageal ulcers. Dermatologic reactions include maculopapular and erythematous rashes, fixed drug eruption, exfoliative dermatitis (uncommon), allergy, serious skin infections, and photosensitivity. Hepatic adverse effects such as liver dysfunction and hepatotoxicity have been reported rarely. Dental effects include permanent tooth discoloration and enamel hypoplasia (especially when used during tooth development), as well as superficial, reversible discoloration of adult permanent dentition. Renal toxicity manifested as a rise in BUN has been reported and is dose-related. Other reported side effects include blood disorders, anxiety, headache, hypertension, dry mouth, back pain, superinfections (including oral candidiasis/oral thrush), and hypersensitivity reactions (e.g., urticaria, angioedema).
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Patients should complete the full course of therapy, even if symptoms improve, and not stop abruptly or without consulting a doctor. Do not exceed the recommended dosage or use for longer than prescribed. Follow the doctor’s instructions for administration time; it is recommended to take the capsule one hour before meals. Take missed doses as soon as remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose. It is recommended to take this medicine with milk or water, and to drink plenty of water (note: milk may reduce absorption of tetracyclines due to chelation with calcium; water is generally preferred). Avoid concomitant use with penicillin due to drug interaction. Do not take with alcohol or caffeinated drinks. Use with caution in patients with kidney diseases or liver impairment; a rise in BUN has been reported and is dose-related, though doxycycline usually does not lead to excessive accumulation in patients with renal impairment at recommended doses. Caution is also advised in patients with Myasthenia Gravis. Patients should avoid exposure to direct sunlight or UV light due to the risk of photosensitivity. There is a risk of superinfection and oral candidiasis. Permanent tooth discoloration and enamel hypoplasia can occur, especially when the drug is used during tooth development. Rapid intravenous administration should be avoided, and prolonged intravenous therapy may result in thrombophlebitis. Inform your doctor about any allergies or pre-existing medical conditions, and if your condition worsens or shows no improvement. Do not drive immediately after taking this medicine.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: This drug is contraindicated in persons who have shown hypersensitivity to doxycycline or any other tetracycline. It is also contraindicated during pregnancy and lactation. Patients suffering from severe liver diseases should not take this medicine.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Oral therapy should be instituted as soon as possible, with parenteral therapy reserved for when oral therapy is not indicated. For adults, the usual intravenous dosage is 200 mg on the first day of treatment, administered in one or two infusions. Subsequent daily dosage is 100 to 200 mg, depending upon the severity of infection, with 200 mg administered in one or two infusions. Exceeding the recommended dosage may increase side effects. Studies indicate that doxycycline at usual recommended doses does not lead to excessive antibiotic accumulation in patients with renal impairment. Patients should follow the specific instructions given by their doctor regarding dose timing and administration, typically taking the capsule one hour before meals.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Primarily indicated for the treatment of Nausea and Vomiting of Pregnancy (NVP).
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: The exact mechanism of action of doxylamine succinate and pyridoxine hydrochloride delayed-release tablets is unknown.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common adverse reactions include somnolence (drowsiness), dizziness, and blurred vision. Other reported side effects include myasthenia, confusion, palpitations, impaired cognition, hallucinations, urinary retention, constipation, sinus tachycardia, agitation, insomnia, headache, fatigue, weakness, restlessness, abdominal pain, diarrhea, mood changes, and troubled urination.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Not recommended for use in females younger than 18 years of age. This medication may cause significant drowsiness (somnolence) and dizziness. Patients should avoid activities requiring mental alertness, such as driving or operating heavy machinery, until they know how the medicine affects them, as there is a risk of falls or other accidents. Avoid concomitant use of alcohol, marijuana, opioids, other antihistamines, and sleeping pills, as they can intensify CNS depressant effects and increase the risk of adverse reactions and accidents. While considered safe for use during pregnancy, consultation with a healthcare provider is recommended for a comprehensive assessment. This medication is contraindicated or not recommended for use in lactating females due to undetermined effects on nursing infants. Patients with a medical history of asthma, glaucoma, stomach ulcer, urinary issues, or blockage of the stomach should inform their doctor before using this medicine. Patients with kidney disease should generally avoid using doxylamine; caution is advised, and consultation with a doctor is necessary, as high doses may lead to kidney impairment. Patients with liver disease should consult their doctor before using this medicine, as high doses may lead to liver impairment. Consult a healthcare provider if taking any vitamins, nutritional supplements, or herbal products. Do not alter the prescribed dosage. Do not crush or chew the tablet; swallow it whole. Do not discontinue the medicine without consulting your doctor. If any swelling is experienced, seek immediate medical attention.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to doxylamine succinate, other ethanolamine derivative antihistamines, pyridoxine hydrochloride, or any inactive ingredient in the formulation. Concomitant use with Monoamine Oxidase (MAO) inhibitors, as they can intensify and prolong adverse central nervous system effects. Not recommended for use in lactating females.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines:
The dosage should be initiated and titrated based on symptom control, up to a maximum of four tablets daily.
*   **Initial Dose (Day 1):** Take two tablets orally at bedtime.
*   **Titration Schedule:**
    *   If symptoms are adequately controlled on Day 2, continue taking two tablets daily at bedtime.
    *   If symptoms persist into the afternoon of Day 2, take the usual two tablets at bedtime, then increase to three tablets daily starting on Day 3 (one tablet in the morning and two tablets at bedtime).
    *   If three tablets adequately control symptoms on Day 4, continue taking three tablets daily.
    *   Otherwise, increase to the maximum recommended dose of four tablets daily starting on Day 4 (one tablet in the morning, one tablet mid-afternoon, and two tablets at bedtime).
*   **Administration:** Do not exceed four tablets per day. Take exactly as prescribed. Take on an empty stomach with a glass of water to avoid delayed onset of action and reduced absorption. Do not alter the dosage without informing your doctor. Do not crush or chew the tablet; swallow it whole. Take at the same time each day. This medicine is a daily prescription and should not be skipped even if symptoms improve; do not quit without consulting your doctor. clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Caution is advised for children with a febrile illness (sudden onset fever of unknown cause) presenting with collapse and shock-like state after vaccination, those with a familial history of Epilepsy (neurologic disorder due to abnormal electrical activity in brain), individuals with bleeding disorders (bleeding and clotting problems), and those with a history of severe local reaction (skin eruptions or injection site soreness) or persistent crying for up to 3 hours after the vaccine. Pregnant and lactating individuals should consult their doctor before receiving this vaccine to ensure safety for the baby.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: This vaccine is contraindicated in cases of acute illness (sudden onset illness), a history of convulsions (a sudden irregular movement of the body due to muscle twitching) commonly associated with brain disorders like epilepsy (abnormal electrical activity in the brain) or the presence of toxins in the body (e.g., in high-grade fever). It should also be avoided in individuals with a previously experienced severe reaction to a similar vaccine, thrombocytopenia (low blood-platelet count), or other neurological disturbances.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Administered to children up to 2 years of age for immunisation. The specific dosage and administration schedule should be determined by a healthcare professional according to national immunization guidelines.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Treatment of type II diabetes mellitus, an endocrine disorder characterized by elevated blood glucose levels due to insulin resistance.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Dulaglutide is a human GLP-1 receptor agonist with 90% amino acid sequence homology to endogenous human GLP-1 (7-37). It activates the GLP-1 receptor, a membrane-bound cell-surface receptor in pancreatic beta cells, leading to increased intracellular cyclic AMP (cAMP) and glucose-dependent insulin release. It also decreases glucagon secretion and slows gastric emptying.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common adverse reactions (incidence ≥5%) include nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and decreased appetite.

Precautions include potential risk of thyroid C-cell tumors, acute pancreatitis, hypoglycemia (particularly with concomitant use of insulin secretagogues or insulin), serious hypersensitivity reactions, acute kidney injury (due to volume depletion), severe gastrointestinal adverse reactions, diabetic retinopathy complications in patients with a history of diabetic retinopathy, acute gallbladder disease, and pulmonary aspiration during general anesthesia or deep sedation. Patients with existing thyroid C-cell tumors, pancreatitis, hypoglycemia, hypersensitivity, or kidney impairment require careful consideration.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Dulaglutide is contraindicated in patients with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) or Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2), and in patients with a history of serious hypersensitivity reactions (including anaphylaxis or angioedema) to dulaglutide or any of its components. It is also contraindicated in lactating women.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Dulaglutide is administered subcutaneously once weekly, at any time of day, with or without food. For Adults: The recommended starting dose is 0.75 mg once weekly. After 4 weeks, the dose may be increased to 1.5 mg once weekly for additional glycemic control. If further glycemic control is needed, the dose can be increased in 1.5 mg increments after at least 4 weeks on the current dosage, up to a maximum recommended dosage of 4.5 mg once weekly. For Pediatrics: The recommended starting dose is 0.75 mg once weekly. If additional glycemic control is needed, the dose may be increased to a maximum of 1.5 mg once weekly after at least 4 weeks on the 0.75 mg dosage. Missed Dose: If a dose is missed, administer it as soon as possible, provided there are at least 3 days (72 hours) until the next scheduled dose.
clinical_profile.black_box_warning: WARNING: RISK OF THYROID C-CELL TUMORS. Dulaglutide has been shown to cause a dose-related and treatment-duration-dependent increase in the incidence of thyroid C-cell tumors (adenomas and carcinomas) in male and female rats after lifetime exposure. It is currently unknown whether dulaglutide causes thyroid C-cell tumors, including medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), in humans, as the human relevance of dulaglutide-induced rodent thyroid C-cell tumors has not been determined.

clinical_profile.black_box_warning: WARNING: SUICIDAL THOUGHTS AND BEHAVIORS. Antidepressants increased the risk of suicidal thoughts and behavior in children, adolescents, and young adults in short-term studies. In patients of all ages who are started on antidepressant therapy, monitoring for worsening and emergence of suicidal thoughts and behaviors is crucial.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Empagliflozin is indicated, in conjunction with diet and exercise, to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus. It is also indicated to reduce the risk of cardiovascular death in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus and established cardiovascular disease.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Empagliflozin is an inhibitor of sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2), the predominant transporter responsible for reabsorption of glucose from the glomerular filtrate back into the circulation. By inhibiting SGLT2, empagliflozin reduces renal reabsorption of filtered glucose and lowers the renal threshold for glucose, thereby increasing urinary glucose excretion. Empagliflozin also reduces sodium reabsorption and increases the delivery of sodium to the distal tubule, which may influence several physiological functions including, but not restricted to, increasing tubuloglomerular feedback, reducing intraglomerular pressure, lowering both pre- and afterload of the heart, and downregulating sympathetic activity.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common side effects include urinary tract infections (bladder discomfort, cloudy or bloody urine, painful or difficult urination), and female genital mycotic infections. Other reported side effects include headache, upper respiratory tract infections, pain in the lower back, blurred vision, rapid heartbeat, confusion, unusual exhaustion or weakness, sweating, vomiting, nausea, gastrointestinal and taste disturbances, abnormal liver function, skin reactions, hepatitis (liver infection), facial swelling, and flatulence. Severe adverse reactions include hypoglycemia (low blood sugar levels), diabetic ketoacidosis, volume depletion, urosepsis, pyelonephritis, necrotizing fasciitis of the perineum (Fournier's Gangrene), hypersensitivity reactions (e.g., angioedema, Stevens-Johnson Syndrome), and reduced Vitamin B-12 absorption.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Assess renal function before initiating treatment and as clinically indicated; empagliflozin is not recommended for glycemic control in patients with an eGFR less than 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 and should be used cautiously in patients with kidney disease. Assess volume status and correct volume depletion prior to initiation. Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) has been reported, including in patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus (for which empagliflozin is not indicated); monitor for symptoms and ketone levels, especially during stress (infection, injury, fever, surgery) or prolonged fasting. Necrotizing fasciitis of the perineum (Fournier's Gangrene), urosepsis, and pyelonephritis have been reported; inform a doctor about any signs of genitourinary infection. Hypoglycemia risk is increased, particularly with concomitant use of insulin or sulfonylureas. Hypersensitivity reactions (e.g., angioedema, Stevens-Johnson Syndrome) can occur. Alcohol consumption is contraindicated as it increases the risk of both high and low blood sugar levels. Withhold empagliflozin for at least 3 days prior to surgery or procedures associated with prolonged fasting. Use with caution in patients with liver diseases, and monitor liver function as abnormal liver function or hepatitis can occur. Inform a doctor about all current medications and significant past medical history, especially kidney/liver problems, alcohol use/abuse, dehydration, low blood pressure, high blood cholesterol, or history of vaginal or penile yeast infections. May cause dizziness and sleepiness; avoid driving or operating machinery until individual response is known. Older persons may be at increased risk for dehydration, kidney issues, and lightheadedness. Do not discontinue this medicine without informing your doctor. Empagliflozin may be associated with reduced Vitamin B-12 absorption. Pregnant females should consult their doctors regarding the benefits and risks, and empagliflozin should only be used if absolutely necessary. Lactating females should also consult their doctors, who may advise stopping breastfeeding or stopping the medicine if absolutely necessary.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to empagliflozin or any of its excipients (reactions such as angioedema have occurred). Not recommended for children. Contraindicated in patients with diabetic ketoacidosis or a pre-coma state. Contraindicated in patients with severe kidney or liver impairment. Not recommended for pregnant females. Contraindicated in patients with heart or breathing disorders. Contraindicated with consumption of large amounts of alcohol.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: The recommended starting dose is 10 mg orally once daily in the morning, taken with or without food. For additional glycemic control, the dosage may be increased to 25 mg orally once daily in patients who tolerate the 10 mg dose. Take the medicine by mouth with a glass of water; swallow whole, do not crush or chew. Take it at the same time every day. Assess renal function and volume status before initiating treatment; correct volume depletion if present. Empagliflozin is not recommended for glycemic control in patients with an eGFR less than 30 mL/min/1.73 m2. Withhold empagliflozin for at least 3 days prior to surgery or procedures associated with prolonged fasting. Store at room temperature, away from sunlight and water, and out of the reach of children and pets. Use exactly as instructed by your doctor.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Empagliflozin + Linagliptin (GLYXAMBI) is used as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Empagliflozin, a component of GLYXAMBI, is also indicated to reduce the risk of cardiovascular death in adults with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: GLYXAMBI combines empagliflozin, a sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor, and linagliptin, a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor. Empagliflozin inhibits SGLT2, the primary transporter for glucose reabsorption in the kidneys, thereby reducing renal glucose reabsorption, lowering the renal threshold for glucose, and increasing urinary glucose excretion. Linagliptin inhibits DPP-4, an enzyme that degrades incretin hormones (glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)). By increasing active incretin hormone concentrations, linagliptin stimulates glucose-dependent insulin release and decreases circulating glucagon levels, both of which are involved in glucose homeostasis regulation.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common side effects include bladder discomfort, cloudy or bloody urine, painful or difficult urination, pain in the lower back, blurred vision, rapid heartbeat, confusion, headache, unusual exhaustion or weakness, sweating, vomiting, and nausea. **Lactic Acidosis (Metformin-associated):** This is a rare but severe, potentially fatal complication. It is characterized by elevated blood lactate levels (>5 mmol/Liter), anion gap acidosis, and nonspecific symptoms such as malaise, myalgias, respiratory distress, somnolence, and abdominal pain. **Genitourinary Infections:** Increased risk of urinary tract infections, urosepsis, pyelonephritis, genital mycotic infections, and necrotizing fasciitis of the perineum (Fournier's Gangrene).

**Hypoglycemia:** The risk of hypoglycemia increases, particularly when used in combination with insulin or insulin secretagogues.

**Lower Limb Amputation:** There may be an increased risk of lower limb amputation.

**Vitamin B12 Deficiency:** Metformin can lead to reduced Vitamin B12 absorption; monitoring may be necessary.

**Hypersensitivity Reactions:** Allergic reactions, including angioedema and Stevens-Johnson Syndrome, have been reported. Inform your doctor if you are allergic to any constituents.

**Stress, Surgery, and Illness:** Blood sugar control may become difficult during periods of physiological stress (e.g., infection, injury, fever, surgery). Patients may experience increased ketone levels if not eating adequately; consult a doctor for potential treatment adjustments and monitoring.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Enalapril maleate is indicated for the treatment of hypertension (all stages, especially where standard therapy is ineffective) and congestive heart failure.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Enalapril maleate is a prodrug that is rapidly biotransformed into its active metabolite, enalaprilat. It competitively inhibits ACE, thereby hindering the production of angiotensin II, a key component of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system. This action suppresses the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, leading to reduced vasoconstriction, decreased renal reabsorption of sodium ions, and ultimately, a reduction in blood pressure and blood fluid volume. It is an orally-active and long-acting nonsulphydryl antihypertensive agent.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common side effects include neutropenia (low levels of white blood cells), hypotension (low blood pressure), rash, loss of taste, chest pain, angina, gastrointestinal upset, blurred vision, and dyspnoea (shortness of breath). Discontinuation rates due to adverse events were 3.3% in hypertension and 5.7% in heart failure patients. The overall percentage of adverse experiences in hypertensive patients was comparable to placebo.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Patients should inform their doctor about all allergies and their past medical history. Patients should avoid alcohol consumption while on this medication. Pregnant females are advised to consult their doctors before taking this medicine. The effect in lactating females is undetermined; consultation with a doctor is advised. While generally safe for driving, patients should be aware of potential hypotension which could affect their ability to drive. This medication is for oral use only; do not self-medicate.

Enalapril maleate is contraindicated in combination with a neprilysin inhibitor (e.g., sacubitril/valsartan), and should not be administered within 36 hours of switching to or from such agents.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Eplerenone is indicated for the treatment of hypertension (high blood pressure), congestive heart failure (including Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction post-Myocardial Infarction), and hepatic cirrhosis with ascites.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Eplerenone selectively binds to the mineralocorticoid receptor, blocking the binding of aldosterone, a key component of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone-system (RAAS). Aldosterone typically increases blood pressure through sodium reabsorption. Eplerenone's action leads to sustained increases in plasma renin and serum aldosterone, consistent with inhibition of the negative regulatory feedback of aldosterone on renin secretion. These increased circulating levels do not overcome eplerenone's inhibitory effects.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Commonly reported side effects include hyperkalemia (high potassium levels) and increased creatinine. Other possible side effects are diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, postural hypotension (low blood pressure upon standing), headache, insomnia, rash, back pain, leg cramps, and renal impairment. In clinical studies for hypertension, adverse reactions were generally uncommon.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Hyperkalemia is a significant concern; serum potassium levels should be measured before initiating treatment and periodically thereafter, with dose adjustments made as necessary. Patients should consult their doctor before taking this medicine if they have pre-existing hyperkalemia or are using potassium-sparing diuretics or potassium supplements. Caution is advised in the elderly, for whom plasma potassium concentration should be carefully monitored before and after treatment. Pregnant and lactating individuals should consult their doctor before use. Alcohol consumption should be avoided while taking this medicine.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Eplerenone is contraindicated in patients with: serum potassium greater than 5.5 mEq/L at initiation; creatinine clearance less than or equal to 30 mL/min; or concomitant administration of strong CYP3A inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole, nefazodone, troleandomycin). For the treatment of hypertension, additional contraindications include: Type 2 diabetes with microalbuminuria; serum creatinine greater than 2.0 mg/dL in males or greater than 1.8 mg/dL in females; creatinine clearance less than 50 mL/min; or concomitant use of potassium supplements or potassium-sparing diuretics.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: For Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction Post-Myocardial Infarction (HFrEF Post-MI): Initiate treatment at 25 mg once daily. Titrate to a maximum recommended dose of 50 mg once daily, preferably within 4 weeks as tolerated by the patient. Dose adjustments should be based on serum potassium levels (e.g., increase dose for serum K+ < 5.0 mEq/L, maintain for 5.0-5.4 mEq/L, reduce for 5.5-5.9 mEq/L, and hold/discontinue for >= 6.0 mEq/L). For Hypertension: The recommended starting dose is 50 mg once daily, administered alone or in combination with other antihypertensive agents. For an inadequate response, the dose may be increased to 50 mg twice daily. Higher dosages are not recommended. For all patients, measure serum potassium before starting eplerenone and periodically thereafter.

clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Epogen stimulates erythropoiesis by the same mechanism as endogenous erythropoietin.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Serious adverse reactions include increased mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, venous thromboembolism, thrombosis of vascular access, increased risk of tumor progression or recurrence (in cancer patients), hypertension, seizures, pure red cell aplasia (PRCA), serious allergic reactions, and severe cutaneous reactions. Other reported adverse reactions include: arthralgia, muscle spasm, pyrexia, dizziness, medical device malfunction, vascular occlusion, upper respiratory tract infection, nausea/vomiting, yellowing eyes/skin, vision changes, trouble sleeping, blood clots, rapid breathing, chest/jaw/left arm pain, unusual sweating, trouble speaking, weakness on one side of the body, fainting, severe dizziness, rash, trouble breathing, itching, swelling, and severe pain (especially in high concentrations).
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Patients, especially those with chronic kidney disease (CKD), experienced greater risks for death, serious adverse cardiovascular reactions, and stroke when administered erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs) to target a hemoglobin level greater than 11 g/dL. Before initiating treatment, evaluate and maintain iron repletion and correct or exclude other causes of anemia. Other serious warnings include hypertension, seizures, PRCA, serious allergic reactions, and severe cutaneous reactions. Consult your doctor before using epoetin alfa during pregnancy or lactation for a better analysis; single-dose vials should be used in these populations as multiple-dose vials contain benzyl alcohol. Its use has shown a risk of drowsiness; therefore, avoid using it while driving. Consult your doctor before using epoetin alfa if you have liver disease or kidney disease. The use of alcohol should be limited or avoided while using epoetin alfa. Patients who are allergic to epoetin alfa or any of its components should consult the doctor before taking it. If taking any vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products, consult the doctor before using epoetin alfa. If any sort of swelling is experienced, consult your doctor immediately. Using epoetin alfa, especially in high concentrations, might result in severe pain.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Contraindicated in patients with uncontrolled hypertension, pure red cell aplasia (PRCA) that begins after treatment with Epogen or other erythropoietin protein drugs, or serious allergic reactions to Epogen. Multiple-dose vials containing benzyl alcohol are contraindicated in neonates, infants, pregnant women, and lactating women.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Evaluate iron status before and during treatment and maintain iron repletion. Correct or exclude other causes of anemia before initiating treatment. In pregnant women, lactating women, neonates, and infants, use only single-dose vials. For patients with Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD): The initial dose is 50 to 100 Units/kg 3 times weekly for adults and 50 Units/kg 3 times weekly for pediatric patients. Individualize the maintenance dose. The intravenous route is recommended for patients on hemodialysis. For patients on Zidovudine due to HIV infection: 100 Units/kg 3 times weekly. For patients with Cancer on Chemotherapy: 40,000 Units weekly or 150 Units/kg 3 times weekly for adults; 600 Units/kg intravenously weekly for pediatric patients ≥ 5 years. For Surgery Patients: 300 Units/kg per day daily for 15 days or 600 Units/kg weekly.
