clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: N/A
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Angina pain, cardiac arrhythmias, palpitation, skeletal muscle cramps, tachycardia, diarrhea, vomiting, tremors, excitability, insomnia, headaches, flushing, weight loss, muscle weakness, sweating, rash, pruritus, edema, restlessness, menstrual irregularity, pseudotumor cerebri (pressure development in the brain), heat intolerance, and transient alopecia.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Caution is advised in people with cardiovascular disorders, diabetes, a long history of hypothyroidism, adrenal insufficiency (where the adrenal gland is unable to produce sufficient steroid hormone), and in aged individuals. Pregnancy: Studies to date have not shown any harmful effects, however, it is recommended to consult your healthcare provider for advice. Lactation: This medication may be safe for lactating females; however, it is recommended to consult your healthcare provider for further advice.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Lidocaine is used as a local anesthetic to prevent and relieve pain and numb local areas during various medical and dental procedures, including numbing the lining of the mouth, throat, or nose.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Not specified in the provided data.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Systemic adverse experiences are generally dose-related and may result from excessive dosage, rapid absorption, inadvertent intravascular injection, or from hypersensitivity, idiosyncrasy, or diminished tolerance. Common adverse effects include dizziness, confusion, convulsions, and depressed respiratory rate. Central Nervous System (CNS) manifestations can be excitatory or depressant, characterized by lightheadedness, nervousness, apprehension, euphoria, dizziness, drowsiness, tinnitus, blurred or double vision, vomiting, sensations of heat/cold/numbness, twitching, tremors, unconsciousness, and respiratory depression or arrest. Excitatory manifestations may be brief or absent.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Patients should consult their doctor regarding use during pregnancy as no definite data is available, and during lactation as the effect is undetermined in nursing females. Driving should be avoided as the medicine may affect the ability to drive. Alcohol consumption should be avoided. Special precautions are necessary for elderly patients and individuals with renal (kidney) impairment, hepatic (liver) impairment, hypotension (low blood pressure), severe shock, epilepsy, myasthenia gravis, porphyria, respiratory impairment, sinus bradycardia (slow heart beat), or any form of heart block. There have been adverse event reports of chondrolysis in patients receiving intra-articular infusions of local anesthetics; lidocaine is not approved for this specific use. When larger volumes are required, solutions containing epinephrine should be used unless vasopressor drugs are contraindicated.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Lidocaine is contraindicated in patients with a known history of hypersensitivity to local anesthetics of the amide type.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Dosage recommendations are typically provided in tables for various types of anesthetic procedures, serving as a guide for normal healthy adults using epinephrine-free solutions. Actual volumes and concentrations must be individualized based on the type and extent of the surgical procedure, desired depth of anesthesia, and patient-specific factors. For larger required volumes, solutions containing epinephrine should be used, unless vasopressor drugs are contraindicated. Lidocaine is not approved for intra-articular infusions.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: This medicine is used as a local anesthetic to prevent and relieve pain during various medical procedures. It is also used to numb the lining of the mouth, throat, or nose before certain medical interventions.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: N/A
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Patients using this medication may experience dizziness, confusion, convulsions, and a depressed respiratory rate. Should any of these symptoms persist for a prolonged period, medical consultation is advised.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Pregnancy: No definite data regarding use during pregnancy is available; consultation with a doctor is advised. Precautions: Caution is advised for elderly patients, and those with renal (kidney) impairment, hepatic (liver) impairment, hypotension (low blood pressure), or respiratory impairment. These patients should consult their doctor before using this medicine.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: This medication is contraindicated or requires extreme caution in patients with severe shock, epilepsy (brain disorder causing seizures), myasthenia gravis (serious muscle weakness), porphyria (a group of liver disorders), sinus bradycardia (slow heartbeat), or any form of heart block. clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Dosage and administration details are not provided in the available data for this combination.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Lignocaine with adrenaline is used as a local anesthetic agent for various procedures.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Lidocaine (lignocaine) is an amide-type local anesthetic that stabilizes the neuronal membrane by inhibiting the ionic fluxes required for the initiation and conduction of nerve impulses, thereby producing local anesthetic action. Adrenaline (epinephrine) is a vasoconstrictor that prolongs the anesthetic effect, reduces systemic absorption of lidocaine, and decreases bleeding at the injection site.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Patients using this medication may experience dizziness, confusion, convulsions, and depressed respiratory rate. If any of these symptoms persist for a long period, a doctor should be consulted.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: This medication should be used with extreme caution in patients suffering from renal impairment (kidney disorder), hepatic impairment (liver disorder), and severe hypotensive shock. Pregnant and lactating women should consult their doctor before taking this medicine. Patients should avoid driving and consuming alcohol when taking this medicine as it may affect their ability to drive and cause adverse interactions.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to amide-type local anesthetics (e.g., lidocaine) or epinephrine. Use in areas with end-arterial supply (e.g., digits, nose, ears, penis) due to the risk of ischemia and necrosis. Contraindicated in patients with certain cardiovascular conditions where vasoconstrictors are not advisable (e.g., uncontrolled hypertension, severe coronary artery disease, pheochromocytoma, narrow-angle glaucoma).
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Dosage must be individualized and depends on the area to be anesthetized, the vascularity of the tissues, the number of neuronal segments to be blocked, the depth of anesthesia required, the individual tolerance, and the technique of anesthesia. The lowest effective dosage should be used. For adults, the maximum recommended dose of lidocaine with epinephrine is typically 7 mg/kg body weight, not to exceed 500 mg in a single setting. Common concentrations include 1% or 2% lidocaine with epinephrine 1:100,000 or 1:200,000.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Indicated for painful gums associated with teething. As a local anesthetic, it is also used for various anesthetic procedures, though specific indications beyond teething are not provided for the benzyl alcohol formulation in the local context.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Lidocaine (lignocaine) is an amide-type local anesthetic that stabilizes the neuronal membrane by inhibiting the ionic fluxes required for the initiation and conduction of impulses, thereby effecting local anesthetic action. Benzyl alcohol may also contribute to local anesthetic effects.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Adverse effects are generally dose-related and may result from high plasma levels due to excessive dosage, rapid absorption, inadvertent intravascular injection, or patient hypersensitivity/idiosyncrasy. Serious adverse effects are typically systemic and include Central Nervous System (CNS) manifestations such as lightheadedness, nervousness, apprehension, euphoria, confusion, dizziness, drowsiness, tinnitus, blurred or double vision, vomiting, sensations of heat/cold/numbness, twitching, tremors, convulsions, unconsciousness, respiratory depression, and arrest. Excitatory CNS manifestations may be brief or absent.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Caution is advised to avoid systemic adverse reactions which can arise from high plasma levels due to excessive dosage, rapid absorption, or inadvertent intravascular injection. A significant warning associated with lidocaine is the report of chondrolysis in patients receiving intra-articular infusions of local anesthetics, for which lidocaine is not approved. Appropriate clinical judgment is crucial when determining dosage and administration.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Contraindicated in patients with a known history of hypersensitivity to local anesthetics of the amide type (e.g., lidocaine).
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: For painful gums associated with teething (local indication), specific dosage guidelines are not provided in the local Pakistani data; however, caution should be exercised to prevent excessive systemic absorption. For other local anesthetic procedures, recommended volumes and concentrations for Lidocaine Hydrochloride Injection, USP vary based on the type and extent of the surgical procedure, depth of anesthesia, and individual patient factors. These dosages are typically for normal healthy adults and may involve epinephrine-free or epinephrine-containing solutions depending on volume requirements and contraindications to vasopressors. These serve as a guide, and actual use must be individualized by a healthcare professional.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Lincomycin is indicated for treating serious bacterial infections, particularly those caused by gram-positive bacteria.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Lincomycin inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding to the 23S RNA of the 50S subunit of the bacterial ribosome, predominantly acting as bacteriostatic in vitro.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common gastrointestinal side effects include persistent diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, glossitis, stomatitis, abdominal pain, abdominal discomfort, and anal pruritus. Severe gastrointestinal effects include colitis (inflammation of the colon), pseudomembranous colitis, and Clostridioides difficile colitis, which may necessitate immediate discontinuation. Dermatological reactions can include rash, urticaria, pruritus, and more severe conditions such as toxic epidermal necrolysis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, bullous dermatitis, exfoliative dermatitis, and erythema multiforme. Hematologic disorders like pancytopenia, agranulocytosis, aplastic anemia, leukopenia, neutropenia, and thrombocytopenic purpura have been reported. Immune system disorders may include anaphylactic reactions, angioedema, and serum sickness. Hepatic effects include jaundice, abnormal liver function tests, and increased transaminases. Renal impairment and vaginal infections have also been observed.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Lincomycin therapy is associated with severe colitis, including pseudomembranous colitis and Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD), which can range from mild to fatal. If significant diarrhea occurs, the medication should be discontinued immediately. There is no definitive data regarding the use of lincomycin in pregnancy; therefore, caution is advised, and healthcare provider consultation is recommended. Precautions are necessary in patients with hepatic (liver), renal (kidney), endocrine, or metabolic disorders. Severe hypersensitivity reactions such as anaphylaxis, angioedema, and serum sickness can occur. Serious dermatological reactions, including toxic epidermal necrolysis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, bullous dermatitis, exfoliative dermatitis, and erythema multiforme, have been reported.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Lincomycin is contraindicated in patients with a known hypersensitivity to lincomycin or clindamycin. It is also contraindicated in nursing females due to the lack of definitive safety data and potential risks.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Lincomycin should be discontinued immediately if significant diarrhea occurs. For intramuscular administration in adults with serious infections, the dose is 600 mg (2 mL) every 24 hours; for more severe infections, 600 mg (2 mL) every 12 hours or more frequently. For pediatric patients over 1 month of age with serious infections, the intramuscular dose is 10 mg/kg (5 mg/lb) every 24 hours; for more severe infections, 10 mg/kg (5 mg/lb) every 12 hours or more frequently. For intravenous administration in adults, the dose is determined by infection severity: serious infections typically require 600 mg (2 mL) to 1 gram every 8 to 12 hours. For more severe infections, these doses may be increased, with daily intravenous doses of up to 8 grams used in life-threatening situations. Intravenous doses require appropriate dilution before administration.
clinical_profile.black_box_warning: Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD) has been reported with lincomycin, ranging from mild diarrhea to fatal colitis. Lincomycin alters the normal colonic flora, leading to C. difficile overgrowth. Due to the risk of severe, potentially fatal colitis, lincomycin should be reserved for serious infections when less toxic antimicrobial agents are not suitable.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Treatment of bacterial infections including: Vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VRE) infections (including concurrent bacteremia), Streptococcus pneumoniae, Complicated skin and skin structure infections (including diabetic foot infections), Uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections, Community-acquired pneumonia (including concurrent bacteremia), and Nosocomial pneumonia.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Linezolid is an antibacterial drug.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common adverse reactions (>5% in adults and/or pediatric patients) include: diarrhea, vomiting, headache, nausea, and anemia. Other reported side effects include: hypertension, insomnia, dizziness, fever, rash, constipation, vaginal moniliasis, and thrombocytopenia.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Myelosuppression (bone marrow suppression) has been reported; patients with uncontrolled hypertension, carcinoid syndrome, or untreated hyperthyroidism should use with caution. For pregnancy: no definite data available, consult a doctor. For lactation: effects are undetermined in nursing females, consult a doctor. Alcohol consumption should be avoided while taking this medicine.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to linezolid or any of its product components. Concomitant use with monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOI) or within two weeks of discontinuing an MAOI (e.g., phenelzine, isocarboxazid).
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines:
Dosage, Route, and Frequency of Administration:
- Nosocomial pneumonia, Community-acquired pneumonia (including concurrent bacteremia), Complicated skin and skin structure infections:
  - Pediatric Patients: 10 mg/kg intravenous or oral every 8 hours.
  - Adults and Adolescents: 600 mg intravenous or oral every 12 hours.
  - Duration: 10 to 14 days.
- Vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium infections (including concurrent bacteremia):
  - Pediatric Patients: 10 mg/kg intravenous or oral every 8 hours.

- Uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections:
  - Less than 5 years: 10 mg/kg oral every 8 hours.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Liraglutide is used to control blood glucose levels in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus, as an adjunct to diet and exercise. It is also indicated to reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus and established cardiovascular disease. Additionally, it is used for chronic weight management in obese or overweight adults with at least one weight-related comorbidity, in conjunction with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Liraglutide is an acylated human GLP-1 receptor agonist with 97% amino acid sequence homology to endogenous human GLP-1(7-37). It binds to and activates the GLP-1 receptor, a cell-surface receptor coupled to adenylyl cyclase activation through the stimulatory G-protein, Gs. Unlike native GLP-1, liraglutide is stable against metabolic degradation by dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP-4) and neutral endopeptidases (NEP), resulting in a prolonged plasma half-life of 13 hours, suitable for once-daily administration. This action contributes to the physiological regulation of appetite and calorie intake.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, constipation, vomiting, headache, dizziness, low blood glucose levels (especially when used with concomitant anti-diabetic therapy), gastrointestinal disturbances, fatigue, fever, toothache, anorexia, and injection site reactions. More serious potential side effects include acute gallbladder disease, increased heart rate, acute pancreatitis, acute kidney injury due to volume depletion, severe gastrointestinal adverse reactions, serious hypersensitivity reactions (including anaphylaxis and angioedema), and potential for suicidal behavior and ideation.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Patients should be counselled on the potential risk of **Thyroid C-cell Tumors**; consult a doctor if you or anyone in your family has ever had thyroid cancer, or if you feel a lump or swelling in your neck, difficulty swallowing, or shortness of breath. **Acute Pancreatitis** has been reported; monitor for persistent severe abdominal pain. **Acute Gallbladder Disease** (e.g., cholelithiasis, cholecystitis) can occur. There is an increased risk of **Hypoglycemia** when used concomitantly with insulin or insulin secretagogues; adult type 2 diabetes patients should monitor blood glucose. Liraglutide can cause an **Increased Heart Rate**. **Acute Kidney Injury** due to volume depletion, possibly from severe gastrointestinal reactions, has been reported; caution should be exercised in patients with pre-existing kidney problems. **Severe Gastrointestinal Adverse Reactions** may lead to dehydration and acute kidney injury; patients with pre-existing stomach problems should consult their doctor. **Serious Hypersensitivity Reactions**, including anaphylaxis and angioedema, have been reported. **Suicidal Behavior and Ideation** have been reported with GLP-1 receptor agonists; patients should be monitored for depression or suicidal thoughts. There is a potential for **Pulmonary Aspiration** during general anesthesia or deep sedation due to delayed gastric emptying. **Pregnancy and Lactation**: Liraglutide is contraindicated in pregnant females and research suggests avoidance during breastfeeding; consult a doctor. **Driving**: Avoid driving if symptoms like dizziness or low blood glucose impair ability.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Liraglutide is contraindicated in patients with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) or Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2). It is also contraindicated in patients with a prior serious hypersensitivity reaction to liraglutide or any excipients in the injection, including anaphylactic reactions or angioedema. Pregnant females should not use this medicine.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Liraglutide is administered as a subcutaneous injection once daily in the abdomen, thigh, or upper arm, without regard to meal timing. Injection sites should be rotated. The recommended target maintenance dose is 3 mg daily. Dosing should be initiated at 0.6 mg per day for one week, with weekly dose increases in 0.6 mg increments until the target dose of 3 mg is reached. For pediatric patients, dose escalation may take up to 8 weeks, and if 3 mg is not tolerated, the dose may be reduced to 2.4 mg daily or to the previous tolerated level during escalation. Adult patients with type 2 diabetes should monitor blood glucose levels before and during treatment. Prior to initiation, patients should be trained on proper injection technique. Consult a healthcare provider for storage instructions.
clinical_profile.black_box_warning: WARNING: RISK OF THYROID C-CELL TUMORS. Liraglutide causes dose-dependent and treatment-duration-dependent thyroid C-cell tumors at clinically relevant exposures in both genders of rats and mice. It is unknown whether liraglutide causes thyroid C-cell tumors, including medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), in humans, as the human relevance of liraglutide-induced rodent thyroid C-cell tumors has not been determined.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Lisinopril is indicated for the treatment of hypertension, heart failure, and acute myocardial infarction. It is also used for the prevention of heart attack and stroke.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Lisinopril is an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor (ACEI) that acts by inhibiting the angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE), a peptidyl dipeptidase. ACE catalyzes the conversion of angiotensin I to the potent vasoconstrictor, angiotensin II. Angiotensin II also stimulates aldosterone secretion by the adrenal cortex. The beneficial effects of lisinopril primarily result from the suppression of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS), leading to decreased plasma angiotensin II, reduced vasopressor activity, and decreased aldosterone secretion. This decrease in aldosterone may result in a small increase in serum potassium. Unlike some other ACEIs, lisinopril is not a prodrug.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common side effects may include headache, dizziness, lightheadedness, tiredness, dry cough, low blood pressure (hypotension), chest pain, nausea, diarrhea, and runny nose.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions:
Before using lisinopril, inform your doctor about your complete medical history, especially concerning heart or kidney diseases, diabetes, and a history of angioedema. Do not discontinue this medicine without consulting your doctor. Inform your doctor about all current medications you are taking and if you are scheduled for surgery. 

**Pregnancy**: Lisinopril is contraindicated in pregnancy and carries a Boxed Warning due to fetal toxicity. Discontinue lisinopril as soon as pregnancy is detected, as drugs acting directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus. 

**Lactation**: The safety and effectiveness of lisinopril in nursing females are undetermined; consult a doctor for more information. 

**Driving**: Lisinopril may cause dizziness; avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you. 

**Liver Impairment**: Use with caution in patients with liver conditions; dose adjustment may be required. Consult your doctor for more information. 

**Kidney Impairment**: Use with caution in patients with kidney conditions; dose adjustment may be required. Consult your doctor for more information. 

**Alcohol Consumption**: Avoid alcohol consumption when using this medicine, as it may increase the severity of side effects.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Lisinopril is contraindicated in patients with a history of angioedema (hereditary, idiopathic, or related to previous ACE inhibitor treatment), or hypersensitivity to lisinopril or any component of the formulation. It is also contraindicated in combination with a neprilysin inhibitor (e.g., sacubitril); do not administer lisinopril within 36 hours of switching to or from sacubitril/valsartan. Co-administration of aliskiren with lisinopril is contraindicated in patients with diabetes.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines:
**Hypertension (Adults)**: The recommended initial dose is 10 mg orally once daily. Dosage should be adjusted according to blood pressure response, with the usual maintenance dose ranging up to 40 mg daily. For patients concomitantly receiving diuretics, the initial dose should be 5 mg once daily. 

**Hypertension (Pediatric patients 6 years of age and older with glomerular filtration rate > 30 mL/min/1.73m²)**: The initial dose is 0.07 mg per kg (up to a maximum of 5 mg total) once daily. 

**Heart Failure**: Initiate with 5 mg orally once daily, increasing the dose as tolerated up to a maximum of 40 mg daily. 

**Acute Myocardial Infarction (MI)**: Administer 5 mg orally within 24 hours of the onset of MI symptoms, followed by 5 mg after 24 hours, and then 10 mg once daily. 

**Renal Impairment**: For patients with creatinine clearance (CrCl) ≥ 10 mL/min and ≤ 30 mL/min, the usual initial dose should be halved. For patients with CrCl < 10 mL/min or those on hemodialysis, the recommended initial dose is 2.5 mg.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Hypertension (including as a first-line therapy for high blood pressure), Heart failure, Prevention of myocardial infarction, and Prevention of stroke.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Lisinopril is an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor (ACEI) that is not a prodrug. It functions by inhibiting ACE, a peptidyl dipeptidase that catalyzes the conversion of angiotensin I to the vasoconstrictor angiotensin II. Inhibition of ACE leads to decreased plasma angiotensin II, resulting in reduced vasopressor activity and decreased aldosterone secretion. This decrease in aldosterone may cause a small increase in serum potassium. Removal of angiotensin II's negative feedback on renin secretion leads to increased plasma renin activity.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common adverse effects include dizziness (7.5%), headache (5.2%), dry cough (3.9%), fatigue (3.7%), and orthostatic effects (3.2%), which can manifest as lightheadedness or low blood pressure. Other reported side effects include chest pain, nausea, diarrhea, and runny nose. The hydrochlorothiazide component may lead to dose-dependent hypokalemia and, less commonly, dose-independent pancreatitis. Adverse experiences are generally mild and transient; however, angioedema and excessive hypotension/syncope are severe potential adverse events.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Pregnancy: Lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide are not recommended during pregnancy due to the risk of fetal injury and death. Discontinue treatment as soon as pregnancy is detected. Lactation: The safety and effectiveness of this medicine are undetermined in nursing females; consult a doctor. Driving: May cause dizziness; avoid driving or operating machinery until effects are known. Organ Impairment: Patients with liver or kidney conditions should use this medicine with caution, and dose adjustment may be required. Alcohol: Avoid alcohol consumption as it may increase the severity of side effects. Medical History: Inform your doctor about your complete medical history, especially concerning heart or kidney diseases, diabetes, and angioedema. Medication Management: Do not discontinue this medicine without informing your doctor. Inform your doctor about all current medicines, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements, and any upcoming surgery. Angioedema/Hypotension: Be vigilant for signs of angioedema or excessive hypotension/syncope. Electrolyte Imbalance: Monitoring for changes in serum potassium and other electrolytes is important, especially due to the hydrochlorothiazide component. Drug Interactions: Use with caution if co-administering with aliskiren (especially in patients with diabetes or renal impairment). Do not administer within 36 hours of switching to or from sacubitril/valsartan.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Hypersensitivity to lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, or any component of the product. Patients with a history of angioedema related to previous ACE inhibitor treatment, or hereditary or idiopathic angioedema. Anuria (due to the hydrochlorothiazide component). Hypersensitivity to other sulfonamide-derived drugs (due to the hydrochlorothiazide component). Concomitant use with a neprilysin inhibitor (e.g., sacubitril); do not administer within 36 hours of switching to or from sacubitril/valsartan. Co-administration with aliskiren (especially in patients with diabetes or renal impairment).
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Lisinopril monotherapy is effective at once-daily doses of 10 mg to 80 mg, while hydrochlorothiazide monotherapy is effective at 12.5 mg to 50 mg per day. For combination therapy, lisinopril doses typically range from 10 mg to 80 mg and hydrochlorothiazide doses from 6.25 mg to 50 mg. Antihypertensive response rates generally increase with increasing doses of either component. Dose adjustment may be required for patients with liver or kidney impairment. While lisinopril's side effects are generally rare and dose-independent, hydrochlorothiazide's side effects, such as hypokalemia, can be dose-dependent.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Lithium carbonate is used for the treatment of acute manic and mixed episodes associated with Bipolar I Disorder, as well as for the maintenance treatment of Bipolar I Disorder in patients 7 years and older. It is also indicated for manic depressive states, recurrent depression, and aggressive and self-mutilating behavior.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: The precise mechanism of action of lithium as a mood stabilizing agent is currently unknown.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common side effects include drowsiness, tiredness, increased thirst, increased frequency of urination (polyuria), mild shaking of hands (fine tremor), weight gain, nausea, vomiting, and general discomfort during initial treatment. These effects may subside as the body adjusts to the medication, but if they persist, medical consultation is advised. Serious side effects requiring immediate medical attention include: severe diarrhea, persistent vomiting, unsteady walk, confusion, slurred speech, severe hand trembling, blurred vision, vision changes (such as a growing blind spot or loss of vision, or symptoms suggestive of Pseudotumor Cerebri), joint swelling or pain, discoloration of fingers/toes, cold hands and feet, and slow/fast/irregular heartbeat. Other serious adverse reactions that may occur include Acute Lithium Toxicity, Hyponatremia, Lithium-Induced Chronic Kidney Disease, Encephalopathic Syndrome, Serotonin Syndrome (especially when taken with other serotonergic drugs), Hypothyroidism or Hyperthyroidism, Hypercalcemia and Hyperparathyroidism, and the unmasking of Brugada Syndrome. Patients should report any continuous headache or visual disturbances promptly.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Treatment initiation should ideally occur in a hospital setting. Patients must maintain adequate fluid and salt intake to prevent toxicity. Caution is advised in patients with epilepsy (seizures), a family history of cardiac arrest or sudden death, and in those with mild to moderate renal (kidney) impairment, where dosage adjustments and careful monitoring are necessary. Patients should be monitored for suicidal behavior. Advise patients to report continuous headache and visual disturbances. Withdraw medication gradually to avoid rebound symptoms. Pre-treatment screening should include evaluation of renal function, vital signs, electrolytes, thyroid function, and a review of concurrent medications and pregnancy status. There is no definite data regarding the safety of lithium in pregnancy; consultation with a doctor is essential before use. Lithium may increase serotonin levels, and the risk of Serotonin Syndrome is elevated when taken with other serotonergic drugs; patients should keep their doctor updated on all medications they are taking.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Lithium is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to any active or inactive ingredient in lithium carbonate or lithium citrate products. This medication is also contraindicated or not recommended in lactating females due to potential harm to the infant.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: For adults and pediatric patients over 30 kg, the recommended starting dosage is 300 mg three times daily (tablets or capsules) or 8 mEq (5 mL) three times daily (oral solution). For pediatric patients 20 to 30 kg, the recommended starting dosage is 300 mg twice daily (tablets or capsules) or 8 mEq (5 mL) twice daily (oral solution). Serum lithium concentration assays should be obtained after 3 days, drawn 12 hours after the last oral dose, and regularly until the patient is stabilized. For acute manic or mixed episodes (patients 7 years and older), titrate to serum lithium concentrations of 0.8 to 1.2 mEq/L. For maintenance treatment of Bipolar I Disorder (patients 7 years and older), titrate to serum lithium concentrations of 0.8 to 1 mEq/L. Pre-treatment screening must include evaluation of renal function, vital signs, electrolytes, thyroid function, concurrent medications, and pregnancy status. Dosage adjustments may be required in patients with mild to moderate renal impairment.
clinical_profile.black_box_warning: WARNING: LITHIUM TOXICITY Lithium toxicity is closely related to serum lithium concentrations and can occur at doses close to therapeutic concentrations. Facilities for prompt and accurate serum lithium determinations should be available before initiating treatment and throughout therapy. Regular monitoring of serum lithium levels is critical to prevent toxicity.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Loperamide is used to treat various forms of diarrhea, including acute diarrhea, chronic diarrhea, and Travelers’ Diarrhea. It is also an off-label treatment for chemotherapy-related diarrhea.

Patients should be warned about the significant risks of exceeding recommended dosages due to the potential for serious and life-threatening cardiac adverse reactions. Keep out of the reach of children.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Loperamide is contraindicated in cases of acute ulcerative colitis, abdominal distention, ileus, and invasive bacterial enterocolitis.

Storage: Store in a closed container at room temperature, away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep from freezing.

clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Loratadine is contraindicated in pregnant and nursing females; consult a doctor for further information. clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: The dosage is dependent on the patient’s condition, age, and response to treatment; consult a doctor or pharmacist before use. Alternatively, 5mg may be taken once or twice daily. Do not exceed 10 mg in 24 hours. Once-daily doses should be taken at the same time each day, either in the morning or at night, typically with a glass of water for tablets. The medicine usually takes about 1 hour to start working, with effects lasting around 24 hours. For occasional or mild allergic reactions, taking it for 1-3 days is acceptable, but longer use may be necessary for chronic conditions like hay fever or pollen allergy, as directed by a healthcare professional. Store between 20° to 25°C (68° to 77°F). Do not use if the safety seal around the cap is broken or missing.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Lorazepam is indicated for the treatment of anxiety and sedation. It is also used to treat status epilepticus, a condition characterized by persistent seizures or rapid succession of seizures. clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Not specified in provided data.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common side effects include drowsiness (somnolence), anxiety, agitation, blurred vision, headache, confusion, mouth dryness, constipation, weakness, rapid weight gain, and shaking of hands or feet. More severe adverse reactions, particularly with injectable administration, include respiratory depression, hypotension, and respiratory failure.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions:
Patients should be aware of the following warnings and precautions:

*   **Pregnancy:** Lorazepam should not be used during pregnancy as it has the potential to harm an unborn child. If symptoms such as slower breathing, feeding difficulties, or frequent crying are observed in a newborn, immediate medical consultation is required. Pregnant individuals are advised to consult their doctors.
*   **Lactation:** Lorazepam is known to enter breast milk and can have adverse effects on a nursing infant. Lactating individuals should consult their doctor before using Lorazepam.
*   **Driving and Operating Machinery:** Lorazepam use may impair one's ability to make decisions and react quickly. Patients should exercise extreme caution when driving vehicles or operating machinery.
*   **Alcohol Interaction:** It is not recommended to consume alcohol while taking Lorazepam as it can exacerbate adverse effects such as dizziness and difficulties concentrating.
*   **Hepatic and Renal Impairment:** Individuals with liver or kidney diseases should consult their doctors before using Lorazepam.
*   **Hypersensitivity and Allergies:** Patients must inform their doctor about any known hypersensitivity to Lorazepam, other benzodiazepines, or any other allergies, as inactive components in the product may trigger allergic reactions or other complications.
*   **Medical History:** It is crucial to inform your doctor about your full medical history, especially if you have kidney problems, liver problems, glaucoma, breathing/lung problems (e.g., sleep apnea), mood/mental disorders (e.g., psychosis, depression), or a personal or family history of substance abuse (e.g., overuse or addiction to alcohol or drugs).
*   **Concomitant Medications:** Before undergoing surgery, inform your doctor or dentist about all medications you are taking, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal medicines.
*   **Central Nervous System (CNS) Depression:** Dosage of Lorazepam must be individualized, particularly when used concomitantly with other medications capable of producing CNS depression, to avoid profound effects.
*   **Elderly Patients:** Adverse effects, especially impaired coordination and drowsiness, may be more severe in older individuals. Lorazepam may paradoxically not provide anxiety reduction in the elderly; instead, it can cause symptoms such as mood/mental changes, sleeping issues, increased sexual interest, or hallucinations. Coordination problems, fatigue, and sleeping issues can also increase the risk of falling.
*   **Pediatric Patients:** Lorazepam may not provide anxiety relief in children and can have an opposite effect, eliciting symptoms such as shaking, agitation, or hallucinations. Lorazepam Injection contains benzyl alcohol, which carries specific warnings for pediatric use, particularly in premature infants.
*   **Airway Management:** For intravenous administration of Lorazepam, equipment necessary to maintain a patent airway should be immediately available prior to use.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Lorazepam is contraindicated in patients with a known sensitivity to benzodiazepines or its vehicle (polyethylene glycol, propylene glycol, and benzyl alcohol), in patients with acute narrow-angle glaucoma, and in those with sleep apnea syndrome. It is also contraindicated in patients with severe respiratory insufficiency, unless they are mechanically ventilated and require relief of anxiety and/or diminished recall of events. Intra-arterial use of Lorazepam Injection is contraindicated due to the risk of arteriospasm, which can lead to gangrene and potentially amputation. Furthermore, Lorazepam Injection is contraindicated for use in premature infants.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Lorazepam dosage must never be used without individualization, particularly when co-administered with other medications capable of producing central nervous system depression. For intravenous administration, especially in conditions like status epilepticus, equipment necessary to maintain a patent airway should be immediately available. The treatment of status epilepticus requires comprehensive management beyond anticonvulsant administration, involving observation and support of all parameters critical to maintaining vital function, with readily available ventilatory support.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Treatment of essential hypertension (raised blood pressure) in adults and pediatric patients. Also indicated for diabetic nephropathy (kidney disease caused by diabetes) in type II diabetes mellitus.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Losartan and its principal active metabolite block the vasoconstrictor and aldosterone-secreting effects of angiotensin II by selectively blocking the binding of angiotensin II to the AT1 receptor. Angiotensin II, formed from angiotensin I by ACE, is a potent vasoconstrictor and the primary vasoactive hormone of the renin-angiotensin system. Losartan does not exhibit partial agonist activity at the AT1 receptor and has a much greater affinity (approximately 1000-fold) for the AT1 receptor than for the AT2 receptor.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common side effects include dizziness, lightheadedness, diarrhea, stomach pain, cold, back pain, chest pain, and stuffy nose. Patients may also experience liver function abnormalities, myalgia (muscle pain), migraine, urticaria (red itchy bumps on skin), pruritus rash, hyperkalemia (high potassium levels), hypoglycemia, and renal failure. Rare but severe adverse reactions reported include anaphylactic reactions (life-threatening allergic reaction), angioedema (severe swelling under the skin surface, especially of lips, face, larynx, glottis, throat, and tongue), hepatitis (inflammation of the liver), cough, anemia (lack of red blood cells), hypotension (low blood pressure), renal impairment, and increased blood urea, creatinine, and potassium levels. In cases of overdose, symptoms may include increased heart rate, hypotension, or slow heart rate. In general, treatment with Losartan potassium has been well-tolerated, with overall incidence of adverse experiences similar to placebo in controlled clinical trials.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Use with caution in patients with renal impairment, hepatic impairment, intravascular volume depletion (e.g., those on diuretics), renal artery stenosis (narrowing), kidney transplantation, primary aldosteronism (hormonal disorder leading to high blood pressure), severe heart failure, aortic stenosis (narrowing), arrhythmias (abnormal heart rhythm), cardiomyopathy (heart muscle weakness), and those with a history of angioedema. Monitor serum potassium levels, especially in elderly patients and those with renal impairment. Avoid consuming alcohol, as it can further lower blood pressure. Patients should inform their doctor about any other medical conditions or medications they are taking. Avoid unnecessary exposure to sunlight; use sunscreen and eyeshades as this medicine can increase sun sensitivity. Store at room temperature, away from direct heat and sunlight, out of reach of children and pets. Caution should be exercised when driving or operating machinery due to potential dizziness.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Losartan potassium is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity or allergy to Losartan or any other components of the product. It is also contraindicated in pregnant and lactating women due to potential harm to the unborn baby and unknown passage into breast milk. Do not co-administer aliskiren with Losartan potassium in patients with diabetes.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Losartan potassium should be administered orally, usually once daily, with or without food. It is recommended to take the medication at the same time each day to maintain consistent drug levels. Dosing must be individualized. The usual starting dose for adult hypertensive patients is 50 mg once daily. For patients with possible depletion of intravascular volume (e.g., those treated with diuretics) or a history of hepatic impairment, a lower starting dose of 25 mg once daily is recommended. Total daily doses can range from 25 mg to 100 mg, administered once or twice daily. If blood pressure is not adequately controlled with Losartan potassium alone, a low dose of a diuretic (such as hydrochlorothiazide) may be added for an additive effect. No initial dosage adjustment is necessary for elderly patients or for patients with renal impairment, including those on dialysis.
clinical_profile.black_box_warning: WARNING: FETAL TOXICITY. When pregnancy is detected, discontinue Losartan potassium as soon as possible. Drugs that act directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus.

clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions:
Pregnancy: This medicine is absolutely contraindicated in pregnant females due to the risk of fetal toxicity, which can cause injury and death to the developing fetus. Discontinue as soon as pregnancy is detected.
Lactation: This medicine is contraindicated in lactating females.
Renal Impairment: Patients with renal impairment (including those with renal artery stenosis, kidney transplantation, and severe heart failure) should be treated with caution. Monitor serum potassium levels, especially in the elderly and those with renal impairment.
Hepatic Impairment: Patients with hepatic impairment require caution; a lower starting dose may be necessary.
Intravascular Volume Depletion: Patients who are intravascularly volume-depleted (e.g., those treated with diuretics) should be treated with caution, and a lower starting dose is recommended to avoid symptomatic hypotension.
Angioedema: Patients with a history of angioedema (severe swelling under skin surface) should be closely monitored.
Cardiovascular Conditions: Caution is required in patients with primary aldosteronism, severe heart failure, aortic stenosis (narrowing), arrhythmias (abnormal heart rate and rhythm), or cardiomyopathy (heart muscle weakness).
Pediatric Use: This medicine should not be given to children.
Driving and Alcohol: Exercise caution when driving or operating machinery due to potential dizziness. Avoid alcohol consumption as it may potentiate adverse effects.
General: Do not start this medication without consulting a healthcare professional.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications:
This product is contraindicated in:
- Pregnant females.
- Lactating females.
- Patients who are hypersensitive to losartan, hydrochlorothiazide, or any component of this product.
- Patients with anuria (absence of urine production).
- Patients with hypersensitivity to other sulfonamide-derived drugs (due to the hydrochlorothiazide component).
- Coadministration with aliskiren in patients with diabetes.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines:
Dosing must be individualized based on patient response and tolerability. Combination therapy is generally initiated after a patient has not achieved the desired blood pressure control with monotherapy, to minimize dose-independent side effects.
The usual starting dose of losartan is 50 mg once daily. For patients with intravascular volume depletion (e.g., those treated with diuretics) or a history of hepatic impairment, a lower starting dose of losartan 25 mg is recommended.
Total daily doses of losartan can range from 25 mg to 100 mg, administered once or twice daily. Hydrochlorothiazide is effective in doses of 12.5 mg to 50 mg once daily, with combination tablets typically containing 12.5 mg to 25 mg of hydrochlorothiazide.
If the antihypertensive effect measured at trough with once-daily dosing is inadequate, a twice-daily regimen at the same total daily dose or an increase in dose may be considered.
If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered. Do not take two doses at the same time to compensate for a missed dose.
clinical_profile.black_box_warning: WARNING: FETAL TOXICITY. When pregnancy is detected, discontinue losartan potassium and hydrochlorothiazide tablets as soon as possible. Drugs that act directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Treatment of hypertension (raised blood pressure) including essential hypertension. Also used for diabetic nephropathy (kidney disease caused by diabetes) in type II diabetes mellitus.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Angiotensin II [formed from angiotensin I in a reaction catalyzed by angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE, kininase II)], is a potent vasoconstrictor, the primary vasoactive hormone of the renin-angiotensin system and an important component in the pathophysiology of hypertension. It also stimulates aldosterone secretion by the adrenal cortex. Losartan and its principal active metabolite block the vasoconstrictor and aldosterone-secreting effects of angiotensin II by selectively blocking the binding of angiotensin II to the AT 1 receptor found in many tissues (e.g., vascular smooth muscle, adrenal gland). There is also an AT 2 receptor found in many tissues but it is not known to be associated with cardiovascular homeostasis. Both losartan and its principal active metabolite do not exhibit any partial agonist activity at the AT 1 receptor and have much greater affinity (about 1000 fold) for the AT 1 receptor than for the AT 2 receptor.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Patients may experience dizziness, diarrhea, liver function abnormalities, myalgia (muscle pain), migraine, urticaria (red itchy bumps on skin), pruritic rash (pus-filled rash). Rarely, anaphylactic reaction (life-threatening allergic reaction), angioedema (swelling under skin surface), hepatitis (inflammation of liver), cough, anemia (lack of red blood cells), hypotension (low blood pressure), renal (kidney) impairment, and increased blood urea, creatinine, and potassium. In general, adverse experiences reported with the combination are mild, transient, and comparable to placebo, typically not requiring discontinuation of therapy.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: This medicine is contraindicated in pregnant females due to fetal toxicity (see black box warning). It is also contraindicated in lactating females. Caution is advised in patients with renal (kidney) impairment, hepatic (liver) impairment, intravascular volume depletion, renal artery stenosis (narrowing), kidney transplantation, primary aldosteronism (hormonal disorder that leads to high blood pressure), severe heart failure, aortic stenosis (narrowing), arrhythmias (abnormal rate and rhythm of heartbeat), cardiomyopathy (heart muscle weakness), and with a history of angioedema (severe swelling under skin surface). Patients should not drive or consume alcohol while on this medication. Serum potassium levels should be monitored, especially in elderly patients and those with renal impairment. Patients with a history of hepatic impairment may require a lower starting dose (25 mg).
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Losartan potassium and hydrochlorothiazide tablets are contraindicated in patients who are hypersensitive to any component of this product. Due to the hydrochlorothiazide component, this product is contraindicated in patients with anuria or hypersensitivity to other sulfonamide-derived drugs. It is contraindicated in pregnant and lactating females. Do not coadminister aliskiren with losartan potassium and hydrochlorothiazide tablets in patients with diabetes.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Dosing must be individualized. The usual starting dose of losartan is 50 mg once daily. For patients with intravascular volume depletion (e.g., patients treated with diuretics) and patients with a history of hepatic impairment, a starting dose of 25 mg is recommended. Losartan can be administered once or twice daily at total daily doses of 25 to 100 mg. If the antihypertensive effect measured at trough using once-a-day dosing is inadequate, a twice-a-day regimen at the same total daily dose or an increase in dose may be considered. Hydrochlorothiazide is effective in doses of 12.5 to 50 mg once daily and can be given at doses of 12.5 to 25 mg as losartan potassium and hydrochlorothiazide tablets USP. To minimize dose-independent side effects, it is usually appropriate to begin combination therapy only after a patient has failed to achieve the desired effect with monotherapy.
clinical_profile.black_box_warning: WARNING: FETAL TOXICITY. When pregnancy is detected, discontinue losartan potassium and hydrochlorothiazide tablets as soon as possible. Drugs that act directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Loteprednol etabonate is indicated for the treatment of inflammatory conditions of the eye, including post-operative inflammation.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Corticosteroids inhibit the inflammatory response to a variety of inciting agents and probably delay or slow healing. They inhibit edema, fibrin deposition, capillary dilation, leukocyte migration, capillary proliferation, fibroblast proliferation, deposition of collagen, and scar formation associated with inflammation. While glucocorticoids are known to bind to and activate the glucocorticoid receptor, the molecular mechanisms involved in glucocorticoid/glucocorticoid receptor-dependent modulation of inflammation are not clearly established. However, corticosteroids are thought to inhibit prostaglandin production through several independent mechanisms.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common side effects include discomfort, itching, dryness of eye, eye pain, and posterior capsular opacification (which may be a consequence of surgical procedure). More serious adverse reactions associated with ophthalmic steroids include elevated intraocular pressure (potentially leading to infrequent optic nerve damage, visual acuity and field defects), posterior subcapsular cataract formation, delayed wound healing, secondary ocular infection from pathogens (including herpes simplex), and perforation of the globe where there is thinning of the cornea or sclera. Pregnancy risk cannot be ruled out.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Use with extreme caution in patients with pre-existing glaucoma due to the risk of elevated intraocular pressure, and in those who wear soft contact lenses. There is a risk of posterior subcapsular cataract formation, delayed wound healing, and increased susceptibility to secondary ocular infections. Perforation of the globe may occur in areas of corneal or scleral thinning. Pregnancy risk cannot be ruled out; consult a physician before use. This medicine should not be used by breastfeeding mothers.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Loteprednol etabonate is contraindicated in most viral diseases of the cornea and conjunctiva, including epithelial herpes simplex keratitis (dendritic keratitis), vaccinia, and varicella. It is also contraindicated in mycobacterial infection of the eye, fungal diseases of ocular structures, and in patients with undiagnosed red eye.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Shake well for one to two seconds before use. Instill one to two drops into the affected eye twice daily, typically beginning the day after surgery and continuing throughout the first 2 weeks of the post-operative period. Patients should wash hands thoroughly before each use. If other eye drops are being used, advise the patient to wait at least 5 minutes between instillation of Loteprednol Etabonate and other eye drops.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Treatment of schizophrenia in adults and adolescents (13-17 years of age). Monotherapy for the treatment of depressive episodes associated with Bipolar I Disorder in adults and pediatric patients (10-17 years of age). Adjunctive therapy with lithium or valproate for the treatment of depressive episodes associated with Bipolar I Disorder in adults.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Lurasidone is an atypical antipsychotic agent thought to exert its therapeutic effects through a combination of antagonism at dopamine D2 receptors, serotonin 5-HT2A receptors, and alpha2C-adrenergic receptors. It also acts as a partial agonist at serotonin 5-HT1A receptors. Lurasidone has no appreciable affinity for histaminic H1 or muscarinic M1 receptors, which may explain its lower incidence of sedation and anticholinergic side effects compared to some other antipsychotics.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common side effects include somnolence, akathisia, nausea, parkinsonism (e.g., tremor, bradykinesia), dystonia, dizziness, agitation, dyspepsia, vomiting, and sedation. Serious adverse reactions include Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS), tardive dyskinesia, metabolic changes (hyperglycemia/diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, weight gain), orthostatic hypotension and syncope, leukopenia/neutropenia/agranulocytosis, seizures, cerebrovascular adverse reactions (including stroke) in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis, and an increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors (especially in children, adolescents, and young adults when used for bipolar depression).
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis. Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults with major depressive disorder and other psychiatric disorders; close monitoring is required. Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS) is a potentially fatal syndrome; discontinue lurasidone immediately if NMS is suspected. Tardive Dyskinesia, a syndrome of potentially irreversible, involuntary dyskinetic movements, may develop; consider discontinuation if signs appear. Metabolic changes, including hyperglycemia and diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, and weight gain, can occur. Orthostatic hypotension and syncope can occur, particularly at treatment initiation or dose escalation; use with caution in patients with cardiovascular disease or predisposition to hypotension. Leukopenia, neutropenia, and agranulocytosis have been reported; monitor CBC in patients with a history of low WBC count. Seizures can occur; use with caution in patients with a history of seizures or conditions lowering the seizure threshold. May impair judgment, thinking, or motor skills; patients should be cautioned about operating hazardous machinery. Disruption of body temperature regulation may occur. Esophageal dysmotility and aspiration have been associated with antipsychotic drug use. Avoid concomitant use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, clarithromycin) and strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, St. John's Wort) due to significant pharmacokinetic interactions.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to lurasidone or any component of the formulation. Concomitant use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir) or strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, St. John's Wort, phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital).
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines:
Administer orally once daily with food (at least 350 calories). 
Schizophrenia (Adults): Initial dose is 40 mg/day. The recommended dose range is 40 to 160 mg/day. Maximum recommended dose is 160 mg/day. 
Schizophrenia (Adolescents 13-17 years): Initial dose is 40 mg/day. The recommended dose range is 40 to 80 mg/day. Maximum recommended dose is 80 mg/day. 
Bipolar Depression (Adults, Monotherapy or Adjunctive): Initial dose is 20 mg/day. The recommended dose range is 20 to 120 mg/day. Maximum recommended dose is 120 mg/day. 
Bipolar Depression (Pediatric 10-17 years, Monotherapy): Initial dose is 20 mg/day. The recommended dose range is 20 to 80 mg/day. Maximum recommended dose is 80 mg/day. 
Dosage adjustment for renal impairment (CrCl <50 mL/min) and moderate to severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B or C): Maximum recommended dose is 80 mg/day. 
Coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors: Reduce lurasidone dose by half of the recommended starting and maximum doses (e.g., if the normal maximum is 160mg, reduce to 80mg).
clinical_profile.black_box_warning: Elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis treated with antipsychotic drugs are at an increased risk of death. Lurasidone is not approved for the treatment of patients with dementia-related psychosis. Antidepressants (including lurasidone when used for bipolar depression) increased the risk compared to placebo of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in pediatric and young adult patients in short-term studies.

clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: N/A
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Potential side effects include pain and redness at the injection site, fever, irritability, and measles-like, rubella-like, or varicella-like rash.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Patients with an acute febrile illness (sudden onset fever with unknown cause) should defer vaccination. For minor cold and flu symptoms, vaccination should not be delayed. Women must avoid pregnancy for up to 3 months after vaccination and ensure effective contraception during and for up to 3 months following the course. Pregnant or lactating individuals should consult their doctor before receiving this vaccine.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: This vaccine is strictly contraindicated in pregnancy, acute febrile disease (sudden onset illness of unknown origin), immunodeficiency (lowered immunity), and known allergy to neomycin.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: The vaccine is administered to children from 9 months to 6 years of age. It may be used in individuals up to 12 years of age. Specific dosage amount and frequency are not provided in the available data but typically follow standard immunization schedules for live attenuated vaccines.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Mebendazole is used to treat intestinal infections caused by common parasitic worms including threadworm (pinworm), whipworm, and large roundworm. It is effective against most types of intestinal worms and is suitable for adults and children over the age of one year. It is used for single or mixed parasitic infections of the gastrointestinal tract.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Mebendazole is a benzimidazole anthelmintic.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common side effects may include gastrointestinal disturbances such as stomach upset, abdominal pain, anorexia, diarrhea, flatulence, nausea, and vomiting. Other reported side effects include rash, dizziness, fatigue, and headache.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Patients should inform their doctor of any existing kidney, heart, or intestinal disease before using this medicine. Caution is advised for individuals with a history of seizures or those who have undergone intestinal surgery or any medical procedure. It is crucial to complete the entire course of treatment even if symptoms improve, as it takes time to eliminate worms completely from the body. Due to potential side effects like dizziness, fatigue, and headache, it is advisable to avoid operating machinery or performing active tasks such as driving immediately after taking this medicine. Alcohol consumption should be avoided during treatment.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Mebendazole is contraindicated in persons with a known hypersensitivity to the drug or its excipients. It is contraindicated for use in pregnant and nursing females.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: For patients one year of age and older, the recommended dosage is typically a single VERMOX™ CHEWABLE 500 mg tablet taken as a single dose. The tablet should be chewed completely before swallowing. For individuals who have difficulty chewing, the tablet can be placed into approximately 2-3 mL of drinking water in a suitably sized spoon; within 2 minutes, it will absorb the water and form a soft, semi-solid mass that can then be swallowed. This medicine can be taken without regard to food intake. Local guidelines may suggest a dosage of one to three tablets daily, with the specific dosage dependent on the patient’s age, condition, and its severity. Always consult a healthcare professional for precise dosage instructions.

Hypersensitivity: This medication may contain inactive ingredients which can cause allergic reactions. Vision: May cause dizziness and blurred vision.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: None explicitly listed in the provided data. However, individuals with known hypersensitivity to mebhydrolin or its excipients should avoid its use.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Dosage guidelines are not provided in the supplied data. Healthcare professionals should refer to established clinical guidelines or product-specific prescribing information for appropriate dosing.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Used in treating pernicious anemia, various types of anemias (lowered red blood cells), and peripheral neuropathies (nerve disorder).

clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Pregnant females and lactating women should consult their doctor before use as the effects of this medicine are undetermined, though in some contexts, Methycobal 500mcg is noted as safe for breastfeeding mothers.
