Central Nervous System: Tiredness, dizziness (approx. 10%), depression (approx. 5%), mental confusion, short-term memory loss, headache, nightmares, insomnia. Cardiovascular: Shortness of breath, bradycardia (slow heart rate, approx. 3%), cold extremities, arterial insufficiency (often Raynaud type), palpitations, congestive heart failure, peripheral edema, hypotension (approx. 1%). Very rarely, gangrene in patients with pre-existing severe peripheral circulatory disorders. Respiratory: Wheezing (bronchospasm), dyspnea (approx. 1%), rhinitis. Gastrointestinal: Diarrhea.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Consult your doctor before taking this medicine if you have first-degree AV block (heart disorder), heart failure, peripheral arterial circulatory disorder (blood circulation disorder), or diabetes. Use with caution in patients with respiratory conditions due to the risk of bronchospasm/wheezing. Pregnancy: Consult your doctor before taking this medicine. Lactation: Consult your doctor before taking this medicine. Driving: Avoid driving as this medicine may affect your ability to drive. Alcohol: Avoid consuming alcohol when taking this medicine.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Metoprolol is contraindicated in sinus bradycardia, heart block greater than first degree (second- and third-degree heart block, or significant first-degree heart block with P-R interval ≥ 0.24 sec), cardiogenic shock, and overt or moderate to severe cardiac failure. It is also contraindicated in patients with a heart rate < 45 beats/min or systolic blood pressure < 100 mmHg (particularly in the context of myocardial infarction). Hypersensitivity to metoprolol or related derivatives, any excipients, or other beta-blockers (cross-sensitivity can occur). Sick-sinus syndrome. Severe peripheral arterial circulatory disorders.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: For Hypertension: Dosage should be individualized. Metoprolol tartrate tablets should be taken with or immediately following meals. The usual initial dosage is 100 mg daily in single or divided doses, whether used alone or added to a diuretic. Increase the dosage at weekly (or longer) intervals until optimum blood pressure reduction is achieved, as the maximum effect of any given dosage level will generally be apparent after one week of therapy. The effective dosage range is 100 to 450 mg per day. Dosages above 450 mg per day have not been studied. While once-daily dosing can be effective, lower doses (especially 100 mg) may not maintain a full effect at the end of the 24-hour period, potentially requiring larger or more frequent daily doses. This should be evaluated by measuring blood pressure near the end of the dosing interval.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Hypertension (adult and pediatric ≥6 years of age), Angina Pectoris, Heart Failure.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Metoprolol is a beta-1 selective (cardioselective) adrenergic receptor blocking agent. At higher plasma concentrations, it also inhibits beta-2 adrenoreceptors, chiefly located in bronchial and vascular musculature. It lacks intrinsic sympathomimetic activity and membrane-stabilizing activity at therapeutic concentrations. Metoprolol slows sinus rate and decreases AV nodal conduction. Its beta-1 selectivity is evidenced by its inability to reverse beta-2 mediated vasodilating effects of epinephrine in normal subjects and its lesser impact on FEV1 and FVC in asthmatic patients compared to nonselective beta-blockers.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Most common adverse reactions include tiredness, dizziness, depression, shortness of breath, bradycardia, hypotension, diarrhea, pruritus, and rash. Other serious adverse reactions reported elsewhere in labeling include worsening angina or myocardial infarction, worsening heart failure, and worsening AV block.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Patients treated with metoprolol succinate may experience worsening angina or myocardial infarction, especially if the drug is abruptly discontinued. Worsening heart failure and worsening AV block have also been reported. Caution should be exercised in patients with underlying cardiac conditions that could be exacerbated by beta-blockade, such as those with risk for severe bradycardia, greater than first-degree heart block, cardiogenic shock, decompensated heart failure, or sick sinus syndrome (unless a permanent pacemaker is in place). Patients with known hypersensitivity to any component of the product should avoid use.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Metoprolol succinate is contraindicated in patients with severe bradycardia, second or third-degree heart block, cardiogenic shock, decompensated heart failure, sick sinus syndrome (unless a permanent pacemaker is in place), and in patients with known hypersensitivity to any component of this product.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Adult Hypertension: Initial dosage is 25 to 100 mg once daily. Titrate weekly (or longer) to optimal blood pressure. Dosages above 400 mg per day have not been studied. Pediatric Hypertension (≥6 years of age): Recommended starting dose is 1 mg/kg once daily, titrated to response. Do not exceed a maximum initial dose of 50 mg once daily. Angina Pectoris: Usual initial dosage is 100 mg once daily. Titrate weekly based on clinical response. Heart Failure: Recommended starting dose is 25 mg, doubled every two weeks to the highest dose tolerated or up to 200 mg.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Metoprolol tartrate is a selective beta-1 blocker used in adults as an immediate-release formulation. It is indicated for the treatment of hypertension, angina pectoris, and for the treatment of acute myocardial infarction, typically initiated 3 to 10 days post-event to reduce the risk of further cardiovascular events and mortality, especially in patients with coronary artery disease.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Metoprolol Tartrate is a beta-1 selective (cardioselective) adrenergic receptor blocker. This preferential effect is not absolute, and at higher plasma concentrations, Metoprolol Tartrate also inhibits beta-2 adrenoreceptors, chiefly located in the bronchial and vascular musculature. Its beta-blocking activity is demonstrated by (1) reduction in heart rate and cardiac output at rest and upon exercise, (2) reduction of systolic blood pressure upon exercise, (3) inhibition of isoproterenol-induced tachycardia, and (4) reduction of reflex orthostatic tachycardia. The mechanism of the antihypertensive effects of beta-blocking agents has not been fully elucidated, but proposed mechanisms include competitive antagonism of catecholamines at peripheral adrenergic neuron sites, leading to decreased cardiac output, and a central effect.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Most adverse effects have been mild and transient. Common side effects include tiredness, fatigue, and dizziness (occurring in about 10% of patients), and depression (in about 5%). Other reported effects include mental confusion, short-term memory loss, headache, nightmares, and insomnia. Cardiovascular effects may include shortness of breath (dyspnea) and bradycardia (in approximately 3% of patients), cold extremities, arterial insufficiency (usually of the Raynaud type), palpitations, congestive heart failure, peripheral edema, and hypotension (in about 1%). Rarely, gangrene has been reported in patients with pre-existing severe peripheral circulatory disorders. Respiratory effects can include wheezing (bronchospasm) and rhinitis. Gastrointestinal disturbances include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, and dry mouth.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Metoprolol tartrate should not be discontinued abruptly. Abrupt discontinuation may lead to exacerbations of angina pectoris, myocardial infarction, and abnormal heart rhythms, particularly in patients with ischemic heart disease. The dosage should be gradually reduced over a period of 1 to 2 weeks and the patient should be carefully monitored. If angina markedly worsens or acute coronary insufficiency develops, metoprolol administration should be promptly reinstituted. Caution should be exercised in patients with respiratory conditions (due to potential for bronchospasm) and peripheral circulatory disorders.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Metoprolol tartrate is contraindicated in patients with sinus bradycardia (heart rate < 45 bpm specifically for myocardial infarction), heart block greater than first degree (including second- and third-degree heart block, and significant first-degree heart block with P-R interval ≥ 0.24 seconds particularly post-MI), cardiogenic shock, overt or decompensated cardiac failure (including moderate-to-severe cardiac failure post-MI), sick sinus syndrome (unless a pacemaker is present), and severe peripheral arterial circulatory disorders. It is also contraindicated in patients with systolic blood pressure < 100 mmHg post-MI, and in individuals with hypersensitivity to metoprolol, related derivatives, excipients, or other beta-blockers (due to potential cross-sensitivity).
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: The dosage of metoprolol tartrate tablets should be individualized. As an immediate-release formulation, it typically requires administration several times per day. Tablets should be taken with or immediately following meals. For hypertension, the usual initial dosage is 100 mg daily, given in single or divided doses, either alone or when added to a diuretic. The dosage may be increased at weekly (or longer) intervals until optimal blood pressure reduction is achieved, with the maximum effect of any given dosage level generally apparent after 1 week. The effective dosage range is 100 to 450 mg per day; dosages exceeding 450 mg per day have not been studied. While once-daily dosing can be effective, lower doses (especially 100 mg) may not maintain a full effect throughout the 24-hour period, and larger or more frequent daily doses may be required, which should be evaluated by measuring blood pressure near the end of the dosing interval. For acute myocardial infarction, immediate-release metoprolol tartrate is typically administered several times daily, usually initiated 3 to 10 days after the event.
clinical_profile.black_box_warning: A boxed warning exists regarding ischemic heart disease. Abrupt cessation of therapy with beta-blocking agents, including metoprolol, has been associated with exacerbations of angina pectoris and, in some cases, myocardial infarction. When discontinuing chronically administered metoprolol, particularly in patients with ischemic heart disease, the dosage should be gradually reduced over a period of 1 to 2 weeks and the patient should be carefully monitored. If angina markedly worsens or acute coronary insufficiency develops, metoprolol administration should be promptly reinstituted.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Metronidazole is indicated for the treatment of parasitic infections and bacterial infections, particularly anaerobic bacterial infections. It is also indicated in the treatment of inflammatory papules and pustules of rosacea, a chronic facial condition characterized by acne and redness.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Metronidazole, a nitroimidazole, exerts antibacterial effects in an anaerobic environment against most obligate anaerobes. Once metronidazole enters the organism by passive diffusion and is activated in the cytoplasm of susceptible anaerobic bacteria, it is reduced. This process includes intra-cellular electron transport donors such as ferredoxin and transfer of an electron to the nitro group of metronidazole, leading to the formation of a short-lived nitroso free radical. Because of this alteration of the metronidazole molecule, a concentration gradient is created and maintained which promotes the drug's intracellular transport. The reduced form of metronidazole and free radicals may interact with DNA leading to inhibition of DNA synthesis, DNA degradation, and death of bacteria. The precise mechanism of action of metronidazole is unclear.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Serious adverse reactions include convulsive seizures, encephalopathy, aseptic meningitis, optic neuropathy, and peripheral neuropathy (characterized mainly by numbness, paresthesia, or tingling sensation of an extremity). Other reported side effects include agitation, blurred vision, confusion, dizziness, and headache. Gastrointestinal adverse effects include nausea, anorexia, vomiting, abdominal discomfort, diarrhea, an unpleasant or sharp metallic taste, epigastric distress, abdominal cramping, constipation, and pancreatitis. Oral manifestations like furry tongue, glossitis, and stomatitis have been reported. Local irritation and pruritus (localized or generalized itching) may also occur.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Patients taking this medication must be cautious and avoid contact with eyes. Caution is advised in cases of severe hepatic (liver) damage, dyshematopoiesis (abnormal formation of red blood cells), and CNS (Central nervous system) disorders. Inform your doctor about your complete medical history before using this medicine. Consult a doctor before using other antibiotics concurrently. Discontinue consumption of alcohol or products containing propylene glycol during and for at least three days after therapy with metronidazole, as it can cause a disulfiram-like reaction including abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, headaches, and flushing. Do not exceed the recommended daily dose. Do not use for longer than it is prescribed without a doctor’s approval. Do not alter your dosage without a doctor’s approval. If this medicine does not suit you, then stop using it immediately. Store at room temperature away from direct heat and sunlight. Keep it out of the reach of children and pets. Do not use after its expiry date or if the quality seal is broken or missing.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Metronidazole is contraindicated in patients with a prior history of hypersensitivity to metronidazole or other nitroimidazole derivatives. It is contraindicated in pregnant females and nursing females. Do not administer metronidazole to patients who have taken disulfiram within the last two weeks, as concurrent use is associated with psychotic reactions.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Use this medicine exactly as advised by your doctor; do not alter your dosage without a doctor’s approval. For the treatment of anaerobic bacterial infections in adults, the recommended dosage schedule involves a loading dose of 15 mg/kg infused over one hour (approximately 1 g for a 70-kg adult), followed by a maintenance dose of 7.5 mg/kg infused over one hour every six hours (approximately 500 mg for a 70-kg adult). The first maintenance dose should be instituted six hours following the initiation of the loading dose. Parenteral therapy may be changed to oral metronidazole therapy when conditions warrant, with the usual adult oral dosage being 7.5 mg/kg every six hours. A maximum of 4 grams should not be exceeded during a 24-hour period. The usual duration of therapy is 7 to 10 days; however, infections may require longer treatment. Do not exceed the recommended daily dose or use for longer than prescribed without a doctor’s approval.
clinical_profile.black_box_warning: WARNING Metronidazole has been shown to be carcinogenic in mice and rats. Its use, therefore, should be reserved for the conditions described in the indications for use.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Miconazole is used to treat fungal infections, including oral candidiasis (thrush), and gram-positive bacterial infections of the skin and nails.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Miconazole is an antifungal drug.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, upper abdominal pain, dysgeusia (taste disturbances), oral discomfort, local irritation, and crusting of the affected side. Severe adverse reactions, including allergic/hypersensitivity reactions, are possible.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Hypersensitivity reactions are a significant concern. During pregnancy and lactation, miconazole should be used only if clearly necessary and after consulting a doctor, as the risk cannot be ruled out and it is not known if it passes into breast milk. Precautions for oral gel formulation include caution in infants without a developed swallowing reflex and patients with liver disease or dysfunction. For topical application, avoid contact with eyes and mucous membranes (other than the intended oral application for oral gel).
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Miconazole is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity (e.g., anaphylaxis) to miconazole, milk protein concentrate (if applicable to the formulation, e.g., buccal tablet), or any other component of the product. For oral gel formulations, it is contraindicated in infants less than 6 months of age. Topical application is contraindicated on burnt or severely infected skin.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines:
Dosage and administration vary significantly by formulation:

**Miconazole Buccal Tablet (e.g., ORAVIG) for Oral Candidiasis:**
Apply one 50 mg buccal tablet to the upper gum region (canine fossa) once daily for 14 consecutive days. The tablet should be applied in the morning after brushing teeth using dry hands. Place the rounded side of the tablet against the upper gum just above the incisor tooth and hold with slight pressure over the upper lip for 30 seconds to ensure adhesion. Do not crush, chew, or swallow the tablet. Subsequent applications should alternate sides of the upper gum.

**Miconazole Oral Gel (e.g., Daktarin Oral Gel):**
*   **For Oral Candidiasis:** Administer as directed by a physician. The dosage and duration of treatment are determined by the type of fungal infection, patient’s condition, age, and response to treatment. Apply a sufficient amount to coat the infected oral mucosa. Continue use until prescribed to prevent infection relapse.
*   **For Fungal and Gram-Positive Bacterial Infections of the Skin and Nails (as per local data):** Apply to the affected skin area once or twice daily, or as instructed by a doctor. Wash hands after use. Avoid using more frequently than recommended. The dosage is largely dependent on the patient’s condition, age, and response to treatment. Consult your doctor for further information.

**General Storage:** Store at room temperature, away from excess heat, moisture, and out of reach of children.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Midazolam is indicated for sedation before and during minor surgical procedures, induction of anesthesia, and for the treatment of disturbances of sleep rhythm and all forms of insomnia. It is also used for sedation in non-critical care settings and during procedures involving the airway, such as upper endoscopy and dental procedures.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: The specific mechanism of action was not explicitly provided in the source data.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common side effects include increased confusion, hallucinations, headache, somnolence (sleepiness), dizziness, ataxia, anterograde amnesia, gastrointestinal upset, hypotension (low blood pressure), rash, slight tachycardia (high heart rate), vasodilation (widening of blood vessels), dyspnoea (difficulty in breathing), thrombophlebitis (blood clots forming in the legs), and pain at the injection site. Fluctuations in vital signs are frequently observed, including decreased tidal volume and/or respiratory rate, apnea, and variations in blood pressure and pulse rate. Serious cardiorespiratory events and possible paradoxical reactions have been reported, with a higher incidence in patients receiving concomitant central nervous system depressants or those undergoing airway procedures without an endotracheal tube.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Midazolam carries a positive evidence of risk during pregnancy; therefore, consultation with a doctor is advised. The effect of this medicine is undetermined in lactating females, and medical advice should be sought. Patients should avoid driving and consuming alcohol due to potential impairment. Precautions are necessary for individuals with chronic respiratory insufficiency, renal, hepatic, or cardiac impairment. Pediatric patients with heart impairment should receive lower doses, and vital functions must be monitored. Caution is advised for patients with a history of alcohol or drug abuse, Myasthenia Gravis, and in elderly patients. Due to the potential for serious and life-threatening cardiorespiratory adverse events, provision for continuous monitoring, detection, and correction of these reactions must be made for every patient. Excessive single doses or rapid intravenous administration can lead to respiratory depression, airway obstruction, and/or arrest, with an increased risk in debilitated patients, those on concomitant CNS depressants, or during upper airway procedures without an endotracheal tube.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Midazolam is contraindicated in patients with a known hypersensitivity to the drug. It is also contraindicated in patients with acute narrow-angle glaucoma. Benzodiazepines may be used in patients with open-angle glaucoma only if they are receiving appropriate therapy. Midazolam hydrochloride is not intended for intrathecal or epidural administration due to the presence of the preservative benzyl alcohol in the dosage form. It is also contraindicated for use in premature infants because the formulation contains benzyl alcohol.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Midazolam injection is a potent sedative agent that requires slow administration and individualization of dosage. Clinical experience indicates that midazolam hydrochloride is 3 to 4 times as potent per mg as diazepam. Because serious and life-threatening cardiorespiratory adverse events have been reported, provision for monitoring, detection, and correction of these reactions must be made for every patient to whom midazolam injection is administered, regardless of age or health status. Excessive single doses or rapid intravenous administration may result in respiratory depression, airway obstruction, and/or arrest. The potential for these latter effects is increased in debilitated patients, those receiving concomitant medications capable of depressing the CNS, and patients without an endotracheal tube but undergoing a procedure involving the upper airway such as endoscopy or dental procedures.
clinical_profile.black_box_warning: WARNINGS Personnel and Equipment for Monitoring and Resuscitation Adults and Pediatrics: Intravenous midazolam hydrochloride has been associated with respiratory depression and respiratory arrest, especially when used for sedation in noncritical care settings. clinical_profile.unified_indications: Minocycline is indicated for the treatment of various bacterial infections, including respiratory tract, skin and soft tissue, ENT (ear-nose-throat), and urinary tract infections. The topical formulation (ZILXI) is indicated for the treatment of inflammatory lesions of rosacea.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: For its use in inflammatory lesions of rosacea, the mechanism of action of ZILXI (topical minocycline) is unknown. (Note: For its antimicrobial effects, minocycline is a tetracycline antibiotic that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis.)
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common adverse reactions include gastrointestinal (GI) upset (such as diarrhea, with an incidence ≥1% reported in clinical trials), dermatological reactions, and hypersensitivity reactions. Patients experiencing these symptoms for a prolonged period should consult their physician immediately.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Minocycline should be used with extreme caution in patients with impaired hepatic (liver) functions. Patients should seek immediate medical attention if experiencing severe or prolonged adverse effects.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Minocycline is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to any tetracycline or to any of the ingredients in ZILXI (for the topical formulation). It is also contraindicated in patients with renal failure, during pregnancy, and while breastfeeding (lactation).
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: For ZILXI (topical minocycline foam): For topical use only, not for oral, ophthalmic, or intravaginal use. After shaking the can well, a small amount (e.g., a cherry-sized amount) should be expressed onto the fingertips and applied as a thin layer over all areas of the face once daily. Additional foam may be used as needed to ensure the entire face is treated. The topical foam should be applied at approximately the same time each day, at least 1 hour before bedtime. Patients should not bathe, shower, or swim for at least 1 hour after product application. Specific dosage guidelines for systemic minocycline for infectious indications were not provided in the submitted data.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Minoxidil is indicated for the treatment of alopecia (baldness and thinning of hair) in both males and females. For systemic use (oral tablets), it is indicated for the management of severe hypertension in patients who have not responded adequately to maximal therapeutic doses of a diuretic and two other antihypertensive agents.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: For topical use in hair loss, minoxidil may cause an initial increase in hair shedding due to its effect of shifting resting hair follicles to the growth phase; this effect might continue for a few weeks. The specific mechanism for its antihypertensive action or overall hair growth is not detailed in the provided data, but it is identified as a powerful antihypertensive agent.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common adverse effects include dermatologic reactions such as dermatitis (itchy, dry, or redness on skin) and hypertrichosis (elongation, thickening, and enhanced pigmentation of fine body hair, developing within 3-6 weeks and potentially lasting 1-6 months after discontinuation). Initial hair loss or shedding may occur upon starting topical treatment due to hair cycle shifting. Other effects include edema (fluid retention), chest pain, blood pressure and pulse changes, shortness of breath, dizziness, and headache. Serious adverse effects, particularly with systemic use, include salt and water retention, pericarditis, pericardial effusion, and cardiac tamponade.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions:
**General:**
*   **Alopecia Treatment:** Results may take at least 4 months. Do not exceed recommended dosage for topical application; applying more will not increase hair growth but may lead to systemic adverse effects such as lower blood pressure, tachycardia, fluid retention, and other cardiovascular effects. Apply only to the scalp, not on broken or unhealthy skin, and ensure the scalp is dry. Do not dry hair with a blow dryer immediately after application as it may decrease effectiveness.
*   **Cardiovascular:** Minoxidil can cause salt and water retention, often requiring concomitant diuretic therapy. Monitor blood pressure, especially in susceptible individuals or those with pre-existing hypotension. Pericardial effusion and tamponade are serious risks. Angina pectoris may be exacerbated.
*   **Pregnancy:** Not recommended for use during pregnancy; use only if necessary after consulting a doctor and assessing risks/benefits.
*   **Lactation:** Not recommended for nursing females. While no evidence of appearance in breast milk is noted, use after consulting a physician.
*   **Driving:** While some local data suggests it may not affect ability to drive, a risk of drowsiness has been reported, so caution is advised, and driving should be avoided if experiencing drowsiness.
*   **Hepatic/Renal Impairment:** Probably safe, but consult a doctor for a better analysis if you have liver or kidney disease.
*   **Alcohol:** Limit or avoid alcohol use while using minoxidil.
*   **Other Hair Loss:** Do not use for other types of hair loss like patchy or sudden hair loss.
*   **Allergies:** Inform your doctor or pharmacist about any possible allergies.
*   **Age Restrictions (Topical):** Not recommended for individuals under 18 years of age or above 65 years of age for topical hair loss treatment.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Minoxidil is contraindicated in patients with pheochromocytoma due to the risk of stimulating catecholamine secretion. It is also contraindicated in individuals with a history of hypersensitivity to any component of the preparation. For topical use, it is not recommended for individuals under 18 years of age or above 65 years of age.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines:
**Topical Application for Alopecia:**
*   Apply exactly as instructed by a doctor, typically to a dry scalp.
*   Do not apply more than the recommended amount.
*   Do not apply anywhere except the scalp.
*   Results may take at least 4 months to become clinically apparent.

**Oral Tablets for Hypertension:**
*   **Patients over 12 years of age:** The recommended initial dosage is 5 mg given as a single daily dose. Daily dosage can be increased to 10, 20, and then to 40 mg in single or divided doses if required for optimum blood pressure control. The effective dosage range is usually 10 to 40 mg per day. The maximum recommended dosage is 100 mg per day.
*   **Patients under 12 years of age:** The initial dosage is 0.2 mg/kg as a single daily dose. The dosage may be increased in 50 to 100% increments until optimum blood pressure control is achieved. The effective dosage range is usually 0.25 to 1 mg/kg/day. The maximum recommended dosage is 50 mg daily.
*   **Dose Frequency:** If supine diastolic pressure has been reduced less than 30 mm Hg, the drug may be given as a single daily dose.
clinical_profile.black_box_warning: Minoxidil tablets contain a powerful antihypertensive agent that may produce serious adverse effects. It can cause pericardial effusion, occasionally progressing to tamponade, and angina pectoris may be exacerbated. Minoxidil should be reserved for hypertensive patients who do not respond adequately to maximum therapeutic doses of a diuretic and two other antihypertensive agents. In experimental animals, minoxidil caused several kinds of myocardial lesions.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Treatment of symptoms of overactive bladder (OAB) in adults, including urinary frequency, urgency, and urge incontinence. Also indicated for neurogenic detrusor overactivity (NDO) in pediatric patients 3 years and older.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Mirabegron is a beta-3 adrenergic receptor (AR) agonist that relaxes detrusor smooth muscle during the storage phase of the urinary bladder fill-void cycle by activating beta-3 ARs, thereby increasing bladder capacity. Beta-1 AR stimulation has been observed at higher doses.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Most commonly reported adverse reactions include hypertension, urinary tract infection (UTI), headache, nasopharyngitis, dry mouth, constipation, and tachycardia (increased heart rate). Other reported side effects include urinary retention, angioedema, atrial fibrillation, indigestion, palpitations, itching, rash, vulvovaginal infection, vulvovaginal itching, gastritis, joint swelling, gastrointestinal upset, and dizziness.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Caution is advised in patients with a history of QT interval prolongation, stage 2 hypertension, or bladder outflow obstruction. Use with caution in patients with moderate kidney or liver impairment. Blood pressure should be monitored as hypertension can occur. Patients with bladder outflow obstruction are at increased risk of urinary retention. Angioedema, including severe cases, has been reported.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to mirabegron or any inactive ingredients of the tablet or oral suspension. Contraindicated in pregnant or breastfeeding women. Should not be used in severe uncontrolled hypertension (systolic blood pressure ≥180 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure ≥110 mmHg), severe kidney impairment (eGFR < 15ml/min/1.73m2) or patients undergoing hemodialysis, or severe liver impairment.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: MYRBETRIQ (tablets) and MYRBETRIQ Granules (oral suspension) are distinct products and are not interchangeable on a milligram-per-milligram basis; selection depends on indication and patient weight. Do not combine tablets and granules to achieve the total dose. For Overactive Bladder (OAB) in adults, the recommended starting dose of MYRBETRIQ tablets is 25 mg orally once daily, either alone or in combination with solifenacin succinate 5 mg orally once daily. After 4 to 8 weeks, the dose may be increased to 50 mg orally once daily. A recommended dosage for MYRBETRIQ Granules for adults has not been determined. For Neurogenic Detrusor Overactivity (NDO) in pediatric patients 3 years and older weighing less than 35 kg, use MYRBETRIQ Granules with a weight-based starting dose as an extended-release oral suspension once daily; dosage may be increased after 4 to 8 weeks.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD) and other depressive illnesses.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Not specified in the provided data.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common side effects include somnolence (drowsiness), nausea, weight gain, increased appetite, abnormal dreams, confusion, anxiety, insomnia, headache, lethargy, dizziness, tremor, sedation, orthostatic hypotension (sudden low blood pressure on standing up), dry mouth, gastrointestinal (GI) upset, rash, arthralgia (pain in joints), myalgia (pain in muscles), back pain, peripheral edema (accumulation of fluid in the fingers and toes), and fatigue. Rare but serious adverse effects reported include hyponatremia (decreased sodium in the blood) and agranulocytosis (decreased white blood cells). Patients should be warned to report any signs of infection, and treatment should be stopped with blood counts performed if an infection occurs.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Antidepressants, including mirtazapine, have been shown to increase the risk of suicidal thinking and behavior (suicidality) in children, adolescents, and young adults in short-term studies for major depressive disorder and other psychiatric disorders. This risk must be balanced against clinical need, and patients should be monitored for suicidal ideation. Use with caution in patients with liver or kidney impairment (as clearance is reduced), epilepsy, organic brain syndrome (a condition which causes a gradual decrease in brain function), diabetes, angina, heart conduction disturbance, recent myocardial infarction (MI), hypotension (low blood pressure), prostatic hypertrophy (increase in size of prostate), narrow-angle glaucoma, or increased intraocular pressure. Caution is also advised in patients with a history of mania (a condition which is marked by periods of overactivity and delusions) or psychosis. Discontinue treatment if jaundice occurs. Dose increases may be detrimental in patients who develop akathisia (a movement disorder characterized by a feeling of inner restlessness and inability to stay still).
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Mirtazapine is contraindicated in patients with a known hypersensitivity to mirtazapine or any of its excipients. Concomitant use with monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) intended to treat psychiatric disorders, or within 14 days of stopping MAOI treatment, is contraindicated due to an increased risk of serotonin syndrome. Similarly, MAOIs should not be initiated within 14 days of stopping mirtazapine. This contraindication also applies to MAOIs such as linezolid or intravenous methylene blue. This medicine is also contraindicated for use during pregnancy and lactation.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: The recommended starting dose for mirtazapine is 15 mg/day, administered as a single dose, preferably in the evening prior to sleep. The effective dose range for major depressive disorder is generally 15 to 45 mg/day, with a maximum recommended dose of 45 mg/day. Patients not responding to the initial 15-mg dose may benefit from dose increases up to the maximum. Due to its elimination half-life of approximately 20 to 40 hours, dose changes should not be made at intervals of less than one to two weeks to allow for sufficient evaluation of the therapeutic response. Clearance of mirtazapine is reduced in elderly patients and those with renal or hepatic impairment, necessitating careful consideration of dosage in these populations.
clinical_profile.black_box_warning: Antidepressants increased the risk compared to placebo of suicidal thinking and behavior (suicidality) in children, adolescents, and young adults in short-term studies of major depressive disorder (MDD) and other psychiatric disorders. Anyone considering the use of mirtazapine or any other antidepressant in a child, adolescent, or young adult must balance this risk with the clinical need. Short-term studies did not show an increase in the risk of suicidality with antidepressant use in adults beyond age 24; there was a reduction in risk with antidepressant use in adults aged 65 and older.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Prevention of NSAID-induced gastric ulcers. For other uses, such as labor induction or medical abortion, misoprostol is used under strict medical supervision following specific instructions from a physician.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Not explicitly provided in the source data.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common side effects include diarrhea (which can be dose-related, usually self-limiting but rarely profound leading to severe dehydration), abdominal pain, nausea, and headache. Other possible side effects include gastrointestinal bleeding, heartburn, dizziness, rise in blood pressure, vomiting, seizures, neck stiffness, and severe allergic reactions (e.g., shortness of breath, rashes). Uterine rupture has been reported, particularly when used for labor induction.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Patients with a history of heart disease, coronary artery bypass graft, or myocardial infarction should use misoprostol with caution or not at all. Use with caution in patients with inflammatory bowel disease or those at risk of dehydration, as profound diarrhea can occur. Avoid alcohol consumption as it may increase the risk of stomach irritation. Inform your doctor about all existing medical conditions and other medications being taken. Older patients should use misoprostol only upon doctor's consultation due to the potential for serious side effects. Patients with impaired liver function should consult their doctor before taking this medication. Misoprostol is not recommended for use during pregnancy for ulcer prevention due to its uterine contracting properties. It is not known whether Misoprostol passes into breast milk; however, due to potential risk, it is generally advised not to use while breastfeeding. Store at room temperature, away from direct heat and sunlight. Keep out of reach of children and pets.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Known allergy to Misoprostol, any of its components, or other prostaglandins. Misoprostol is contraindicated in pregnant women for ulcer prevention due to its uterine contracting properties and the significant risks of birth defects, abortion, premature birth, or uterine rupture. It is also contraindicated in patients with a history of coronary artery bypass graft or myocardial infarction. Use in nursing females is generally contraindicated due to the potential for passage into breast milk.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: For reducing the risk of NSAID-induced gastric ulcers, the recommended adult oral dose is 200 mcg four times daily, taken with food (with meals and at bedtime). If this dose cannot be tolerated, a dose of 100 mcg can be used. Misoprostol should be taken for the duration of NSAID therapy. For other uses, such as labor induction or medical abortion, dosage should strictly follow specific physician instructions; in some contexts, 4 x 200 mcg tablets (800 mcg total) may be taken at once, with dosage dependent on patient's condition, age, and response. Tablets should be taken by mouth with a glass of water and not crushed, chewed, or dissolved. Vaginal administration may be considered for certain uses (e.g., Breeky tablets), and consultation with a doctor is necessary for such routes. For patients with renal impairment, adjustment of the dosing schedule is not routinely needed, but the dose can be reduced if the 200 mcg dose is not tolerated.
clinical_profile.black_box_warning: MISOPROSTOL ADMINISTRATION TO WOMEN WHO ARE PREGNANT CAN CAUSE BIRTH DEFECTS, ABORTION, PREMATURE BIRTH OR UTERINE RUPTURE. UTERINE RUPTURE HAS BEEN REPORTED WHEN MISOPROSTOL WAS ADMINISTERED IN PREGNANT WOMEN TO INDUCE LABOR OR TO INDUCE ABORTION. THE RISK OF UTERINE RUPTURE INCREASES WITH ADVANCING GESTATIONAL AGES AND WITH PRIOR UTERINE SURGERY, INCLUDING CESAREAN DELIVERY. MISOPROSTOL SHOULD NOT BE TAKEN BY PREGNANT WOMEN TO REDUCE THE RISK OF ULCERS INDUCED BY NONSTEROIDAL ANTI-INFLAMMATORY DRUGS (NSAIDs).

clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common adverse reactions (≥ 20%) include ureteric obstruction, flank pain, urinary tract infection, hematuria, renal dysfunction, nausea, abdominal pain, fatigue, dysuria, and vomiting. Other clinically significant adverse reactions include bone marrow suppression.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Clinically significant warnings include ureteric obstruction and bone marrow suppression. Monitor patients for these serious adverse events.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Mitomycin (JELMYTO) is contraindicated in patients with perforation of the bladder or upper urinary tract.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: For pyelocalyceal use only; not for intravenous, topical, or oral administration. Administer 1.3 g of sodium bicarbonate orally the evening prior to, the morning of, and 30 minutes prior to instillation procedure (total of 3.9 g). The dose to be instilled is 4 mg per mL via ureteral catheter or nephrostomy tube, with total instillation volume based on volumetric measurements using pyelography, not to exceed 15 mL (60 mg of mitomycin). Instill once weekly for six weeks. For patients with a complete response 3 months after initiation, instillations may be administered once a month for a maximum of 11 additional instillations.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Mometasone furoate nasal spray is typically indicated for the prophylaxis and treatment of seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis symptoms in adults and children, and for the treatment of nasal polyps. Note: The provided US FDA clinical data pertains to an *oral inhaled* formulation (ASMANEX TWISTHALER) indicated for asthma, not the nasal formulation.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Mometasone furoate is a corticosteroid demonstrating potent anti-inflammatory activity. The precise mechanism of corticosteroid action on asthma (and presumably allergic rhinitis/nasal inflammation) is not fully known. Inflammation is an important component in the pathogenesis of these conditions. Corticosteroids have been shown to have a wide range of inhibitory effects on multiple cell types (e.g., mast cells, eosinophils, neutrophils, macrophages, and lymphocytes) and mediators (e.g., histamine, eicosanoids, leukotrienes, and cytokines) involved in inflammation. Mometasone furoate has been shown in vitro to exhibit a high binding affinity for the human glucocorticoid receptor, approximately 12 times that of dexamethasone, 7 times that of triamcinolone acetonide, 5 times that of budesonide, and 1.5 times that of fluticasone. The clinical significance of these binding affinity findings is unknown.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Clinically significant adverse reactions described in the FDA labeling (primarily for the inhaled formulation, but relevant to systemic corticosteroid effects and some local effects) include Oropharyngeal Candidiasis (more prominent with inhaled forms), Immunosuppression and Risk of Infections, Hypercorticism and Adrenal Suppression, Reduction in Bone Mineral Density, Growth Effects, Glaucoma and Cataracts. The most common adverse reactions reported in clinical studies (for the inhaled form, incidence ≥5%) are headache, allergic rhinitis, pharyngitis, upper respiratory tract infection, sinusitis, oral candidiasis, dysmenorrhea, musculoskeletal pain, back pain, and dyspepsia. For nasal formulations, local adverse effects such as epistaxis, nasal irritation, and pharyngeal irritation are also commonly reported.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Warnings and precautions for corticosteroids include: Oropharyngeal Candidiasis, Immunosuppression and Risk of Infections, Hypercorticism and Adrenal Suppression, Reduction in Bone Mineral Density, Growth Effects (especially in pediatric patients), and Glaucoma and Cataracts.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: The provided US FDA data lists contraindications for ASMANEX TWISTHALER (an oral inhaled formulation) including its use in the primary treatment of status asthmaticus or other acute episodes of asthma where intensive measures are required, and in patients with known hypersensitivity to milk proteins or any ingredients of ASMANEX TWISTHALER. For mometasone furoate nasal spray, contraindications typically include known hypersensitivity to mometasone furoate or any other components of the nasal spray formulation.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: The provided US FDA data describes dosage for an oral inhaled formulation (ASMANEX TWISTHALER) for asthma, which is not applicable to mometasone furoate nasal spray. Typical clinical standard dosage guidelines for mometasone furoate nasal spray for allergic rhinitis in adults and adolescents aged 12 years and older are 2 sprays in each nostril once daily. For children aged 2 to 11 years, the typical dosage is 1 spray in each nostril once daily. For nasal polyps, the typical dosage for adults and adolescents aged 18 years and older is 2 sprays in each nostril twice daily. Patients should be instructed to inhale rapidly and deeply for effective delivery (when applicable for certain devices) and to follow specific administration instructions for nasal sprays.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Mometasone furoate topical is used to treat psoriasis (an immune-mediated skin condition characterized by red, scaly patches), eczemas (inflammatory and itchy skin conditions), and other inflammatory dermatoses. It is not indicated for the primary treatment of status asthmaticus or other acute episodes of asthma, as the provided US FDA data pertains to an inhaled formulation of mometasone.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Mometasone furoate is a corticosteroid that demonstrates potent anti-inflammatory activity. Its mechanism involves inhibitory effects on multiple cell types (e.g., mast cells, eosinophils, neutrophils, macrophages, and lymphocytes) and mediators (e.g., histamine, eicosanoids, leukotrienes, and cytokines) involved in inflammation. Mometasone furoate exhibits a high binding affinity for the human glucocorticoid receptor, suggesting its potent corticosteroid action.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common local side effects observed with topical mometasone furoate include burning, itching, irritation, stinging, dryness, folliculitis (inflammation of hair follicles), pruritus (itching), hypo-pigmentation, allergic dermatitis, numbness of fingers, maceration of skin, striae (permanent stretch marks), skin atrophy (thinning of the skin), telangiectasia (spider veins), and general local skin reactions. Systemic adverse reactions, while less common with proper topical use, can occur, especially with potent steroids, application over large surface areas, or under occlusive dressings. These potential systemic effects include hypercorticism, adrenal suppression, immunosuppression with increased risk of infections, reduction in bone mineral density, growth effects (in children), glaucoma, and cataracts. Other systemic side effects such as headache, allergic rhinitis, pharyngitis, upper respiratory tract infection, sinusitis, oral candidiasis, dysmenorrhea, musculoskeletal pain, back pain, and dyspepsia have been reported with other routes of administration but are generally not associated with appropriate topical use.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Pregnant females should consult their doctor before using this drug, although there is no definitive evidence of risk in humans. Lactating mothers should also seek medical advice, as the effect on lactation is undetermined or caution is advised. Systemic effects, such as hypercorticism and adrenal suppression, are usually associated with the use of more potent steroids, application over large surface areas, or the addition of occlusive dressings. Prolonged use of topical corticosteroids may lead to clinically significant skin atrophy. Patients should discontinue use if local irritation develops. This medicine should be avoided on mucous membranes, in the eyes, and on broken or inflamed skin. Extensive or prolonged use should be avoided. Other potential systemic risks, especially with inappropriate use, include immunosuppression (increasing infection risk), reduction in bone mineral density, growth effects (in pediatric patients), glaucoma, and cataracts.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Mometasone furoate topical is contraindicated in patients with a known hypersensitivity to mometasone furoate, other corticosteroids, or any component of the formulation. It is also contraindicated for application to mucous membranes, eyes, broken skin, or acutely inflamed skin.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Specific dosage guidelines (e.g., frequency and duration of application) for topical mometasone furoate are not provided in the source data. However, general precautions emphasize avoiding extensive or prolonged use to minimize potential local and systemic adverse effects.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Mometasone topical is used to treat inflammatory and pruritic skin conditions such as eczema, psoriasis, allergies, and rash. It helps reduce itching and inflammation.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Mometasone furoate is a potent synthetic corticosteroid. Its anti-inflammatory properties are mediated through a wide range of effects on multiple cell types (e.g., mast cells, eosinophils, neutrophils, macrophages, and lymphocytes) and inflammatory mediators (e.g., histamine, eicosanoids, leukotrienes, and cytokines). This action reduces inflammation and pruritus in affected skin areas.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common topical side effects include burning, itching, or stinging at the application site, which usually lasts a short time. Other potential local side effects include acne, alteration in skin color, dryness, and skin ulcers. With prolonged or extensive use, particularly under occlusion or on sensitive skin areas, systemic corticosteroid effects, skin thinning (atrophy), striae, impaired wound healing, and increased susceptibility to local skin infections (including Candida albicans infection) may occur.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Avoid applying this medication to the face, underarms, groin, or for diaper rash unless specifically directed by a healthcare professional. Ensure hands are washed before and after application (unless treating hands). Do not get the medicine in the eyes, mouth, or nose; if contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with water and seek medical advice if irritation persists. Inform your doctor about any known hypersensitivity or allergies to mometasone furoate or any of its ingredients. Disclose your medical history, especially if you have poor blood circulation, diabetes, or immune system problems, as corticosteroids can aggravate and complicate skin infections. If a skin infection develops, inform your doctor for appropriate treatment. Prolonged use or application over large skin areas may lead to systemic corticosteroid effects, including hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis suppression, hypercorticism, and growth reduction in children. Inform your doctors or dentist if you are using this medicine prior to any procedures. Caution should be exercised during pregnancy and lactation; use only if absolutely necessary and after consulting a doctor, as it is uncertain whether it is excreted in breast milk. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Store at room temperature away from direct heat and sunlight.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Mometasone topical is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity or allergy to mometasone furoate or any of its ingredients.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: For topical use only. Wash and dry hands before use. Clean and dry the affected skin area. Apply a thin coating of the medicine to the affected area as instructed by your doctor and rub it in gently. Do not rinse or wash off the medicine after application. Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water after each application, unless the hands are the area being treated. The frequency and duration of treatment should be determined by your doctor.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Montelukast is indicated for the control and prevention of symptoms caused by asthma (a chronic inflammatory disease of the lungs, characterized by narrowing of the airways) in patients 12 months and older. It is also used for the acute prevention of exercise-induced bronchoconstriction (EIB) in patients 6 years and older. Additionally, it is used to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis, including seasonal allergic rhinitis (in patients 2 years and older) and perennial allergic rhinitis (in patients 6 months and older), such as sneezing, stuffy/runny/itchy nose, and hay fever.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Montelukast is a leukotriene receptor antagonist that binds with high affinity and selectivity to the cysteinyl leukotriene type-1 (CysLT1) receptor. It works by blocking the action of cysteinyl leukotrienes (LTC4, LTD4, LTE4), which are products of arachidonic acid metabolism released from cells like mast cells and eosinophils. These leukotrienes are involved in the pathophysiology of asthma and allergic rhinitis, causing airway edema, smooth muscle contraction, and inflammation in the airways. By inhibiting these effects, Montelukast reduces inflammation and swelling in the airways, making it easier to breathe and alleviating symptoms of asthma and allergic rhinitis. It is not a bronchodilator or an immunosuppressant.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common side effects include headache, abdominal pain, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, gastrointestinal upset, upper respiratory infection, fever, pharyngitis, cough, influenza, rhinorrhea, sinusitis, and otitis. Less common or serious side effects may include allergic reactions (e.g., rash, itching, hives, anaphylaxis, angioedema, difficulty breathing, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat), agitation, restlessness, hyperactivity, dizziness, drowsiness, muscle weakness, muscle spasm (hyperkinesia), tingling/numbness/weakness in the arms or legs, elevated liver enzymes (ALT/AST), cholestatic hepatitis, and thirst. Symptoms of overdose can include stomach pain, headache, dizziness, drowsiness, hyperactivity, agitation, vomiting, restlessness, palpitations, seizures, hallucinations, and difficulty breathing. Patients should discontinue the medication and seek medical attention if symptoms of Churg-Strauss Syndrome appear (a disorder marked by blood vessel inflammation restricting blood flow to organs and tissues).
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions:
Patients and caregivers should be advised to be alert for the emergence or worsening of any neuropsychiatric symptoms and to seek medical advice immediately if these changes occur.
Montelukast is not indicated for the reversal of bronchospasm in acute asthma attacks and should not be used as a rescue medication. Patients should be advised to have appropriate rescue medication available.
Do not abruptly substitute montelukast for oral or inhaled corticosteroid therapy. Dosage reduction of systemic corticosteroids should be gradual and under medical supervision.
Systemic eosinophilia, sometimes presenting with clinical features of vasculitis consistent with Churg-Strauss Syndrome, has been reported. These events are sometimes associated with the reduction of oral corticosteroid therapy. Discontinue montelukast if symptoms of Churg-Strauss Syndrome appear.
Use with caution in patients with liver disease. Regular liver function tests may be required during treatment. Inform your doctor about any history of liver disease.
Severe allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis, angioedema, and hives, can occur. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience symptoms such as difficulty breathing or swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat.
While montelukast is not known to cause lung infections, people with asthma are at an increased risk of developing respiratory infections, including pneumonia, bronchitis, or tuberculosis. Seek medical attention if symptoms such as fever, cough, or difficulty breathing develop.
Montelukast is not a substitute for non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for individuals with aspirin-sensitive asthma.
Chewable tablets may contain aspartame, a source of phenylalanine. Patients with phenylketonuria should inform their doctor prior to use.
The effects of montelukast during pregnancy and breastfeeding are undetermined, and caution is advised. It should be used only if the potential benefits outweigh the potential risks. Montelukast may pass into breast milk, so breastfed infants should be monitored for potential side effects. Consult a healthcare provider before use if pregnant or breastfeeding.
Montelukast may interact with other medications, including certain antibiotics, antifungal medications, and HIV medications, as well as over-the-counter medications and herbal supplements. Inform your healthcare provider about all medications, supplements, and herbal products you are taking.
Montelukast may cause dizziness or drowsiness; therefore, avoid driving or operating machinery immediately after taking this medicine until you know how it affects you. Alcohol consumption should be avoided.
There is no evidence to suggest a significant impact on fertility in men or women. However, consult your healthcare provider if you are planning to conceive or have concerns about fertility.
Store at room temperature, away from excess heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date.
It is important to follow the dosage instructions provided by your healthcare provider. Do not take more or less than recommended. Do not stop taking the medication without consulting your healthcare provider, even if you feel better. Consult your healthcare provider before starting or stopping any medications.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Montelukast is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to montelukast or any component of this product. Patients with severe heart, kidney, or liver disease, and individuals with Phenylketonuria, should discuss with their doctor for a case-specific treatment plan, as these conditions might necessitate avoidance or careful consideration.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines:
Montelukast should be administered orally once daily. Tablets should be swallowed whole with a glass of water and should not be crushed, chewed, or broken. Oral granules must be administered within 15 minutes after opening the sachet, with or without mixing with food. Take regularly for consistent effect. If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it's almost time for the next dose; do not double dose.

**Asthma:** Administer once daily in the evening.
*   **Patients 15 years and older:** One 10-mg tablet.
*   **Patients 6 to 14 years:** One 5-mg chewable tablet.
*   **Patients 2 to 5 years:** One 4-mg chewable tablet or one sachet of 4-mg oral granules.
*   **Patients 12 months to 23 months:** One sachet of 4-mg oral granules.

**Acute Prevention of Exercise-Induced Bronchoconstriction (EIB):** Administer one dose at least 2 hours before exercise.
*   **Patients 15 years and older:** One 10-mg tablet.
*   **Patients 6 to 14 years:** One 5-mg chewable tablet.
*   An additional dose should not be taken within 24 hours of a previous dose. Patients already taking montelukast daily for another indication should not take an additional dose for EIB.

**Allergic Rhinitis:** Administer once daily. The timing of administration can be in the evening for better control of nocturnal symptoms and adherence, or as directed by a healthcare provider.
*   **Seasonal Allergic Rhinitis (patients 2 years and older):**
    *   **Patients 15 years and older:** One 10-mg tablet.
    *   **Patients 6 to 14 years:** One 5-mg chewable tablet.
    *   **Patients 2 to 5 years:** One 4-mg chewable tablet or one sachet of 4-mg oral granules.
*   **Perennial Allergic Rhinitis (patients 6 months and older):**
    *   **Patients 15 years and older:** One 10-mg tablet.
    *   **Patients 6 to 14 years:** One 5-mg chewable tablet.
    *   **Patients 2 to 5 years:** One 4-mg chewable tablet or one sachet of 4-mg oral granules.
    *   **Patients 6 months to 23 months:** One sachet of 4-mg oral granules.

**Patients with both Asthma and Allergic Rhinitis:** Take only one dose daily in the evening.
clinical_profile.black_box_warning: The US FDA has issued a Boxed Warning for Montelukast due to the risk of serious neuropsychiatric events. These include, but are not limited to, agitation, aggression, depression, sleep disturbances, hallucinations, tremors, suicidal thoughts and behavior. Patients and caregivers should be advised to be alert for the emergence or worsening of any neuropsychiatric symptoms and to seek medical advice immediately if these changes occur.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Control and prevention of symptoms associated with chronic asthma (including prevention of exercise-induced bronchoconstriction), perennial allergic rhinitis, and seasonal allergic rhinitis (e.g., sneezing, nasal congestion, runny nose, itchy nose, itchy watery eyes, itching of the throat or roof of the mouth), and hay fever.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Montelukast acts as a selective leukotriene receptor antagonist, specifically targeting the cysteinyl leukotriene type 1 (CysLT1) receptor to inhibit the actions of leukotriene D4 (LTD4). This helps to prevent bronchoconstriction and reduce inflammatory processes involved in asthma and allergic rhinitis. Fexofenadine is a selective peripheral H1-receptor antagonist that blocks the effects of histamine at H1 receptors, thereby alleviating symptoms of allergic reactions without causing significant sedation.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Commonly reported side effects include abdominal pain, headache, thirst, and general gastrointestinal upset. Other reported adverse effects include hyperkinesia (muscle spasm). Rare but serious side effects include anaphylaxis (severe allergic reaction), angioedema (swelling beneath the skin or mucous membranes), seizures, elevated liver enzymes (ALT/AST), and cholestatic hepatitis (liver injury).
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Pregnancy: The effects of this medicine are undetermined in pregnant females; therefore, caution is advised. Consult your doctor before use. Lactation: The effects of this medicine are undetermined in nursing females; therefore, caution is advised. Consult your doctor before use. Driving: This medicine may affect your ability to drive; avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol: Avoid consuming alcohol while taking this medicine. Precautions: Do not substitute abruptly for inhaled or oral steroid therapy. This medication is not indicated for the relief of acute asthma attacks. Discontinue the medication immediately if symptoms consistent with Churg-Strauss Syndrome (e.g., eosinophilia, vasculitic rash, worsening pulmonary symptoms, cardiac complications, and/or neuropathy) appear. Chewable tablets may contain aspartame; patients with Phenylketonuria or any other condition requiring restriction of aspartame/phenylalanine should consult their doctor or pharmacist before use.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to montelukast, fexofenadine, or any other component of the formulation.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Dosage should be individualized based on patient's age, weight, and clinical response. For adults and adolescents 15 years and older, a common fixed-dose combination typically involves montelukast 10 mg with fexofenadine 120 mg or 180 mg, administered orally once daily. For pediatric patients (e.g., 6-14 years), a common combination may be montelukast 5 mg with fexofenadine 60 mg orally once daily. Always follow the specific instructions and dosage prescribed by a healthcare provider.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Treatment of bacterial conjunctivitis (inflammation of the conjunctiva in the eye) caused by susceptible organisms.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Moxifloxacin is a member of the fluoroquinolone class of antibacterial agents.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common ophthalmic side effects include conjunctivitis, reduced visual acuity (worsening of eyesight), dry eyes, keratitis (inflammation of the eye), eye discomfort, subconjunctival haemorrhage (bursting of small blood vessels in the eye), tearing, pain, redness, and itching. Other reported systemic side effects from local data include headache, dizziness, flushing, swollen ankles, and dysgeusia (distortion of sense of taste).
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Prolonged use of ophthalmic moxifloxacin may lead to overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms. Patients should not use this medicine while wearing contact lenses. Patients with known allergies to moxifloxacin or any fluoroquinolone should consult a doctor before use. If any swelling or signs of a severe allergic reaction are experienced, immediate medical consultation is necessary. Consultation with a doctor is advised if taking any vitamins, nutritional supplements, or herbal products. Caution is recommended for pregnant and lactating women, with medical consultation prior to use. Due to potential drowsiness, individuals should avoid driving or operating heavy machinery. Patients with liver or kidney disease should consult their doctor for a better analysis. Alcohol consumption should be limited or avoided. Although systemic absorption from ophthalmic use is generally low, moxifloxacin, as a fluoroquinolone, carries serious class warnings including tendinitis and tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, central nervous system effects (such as seizures, dizziness, and confusion), exacerbation of myasthenia gravis, QT prolongation, risk of aortic aneurysm and dissection, and Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea. clinical_profile.black_box_warning: Fluoroquinolones, including moxifloxacin, have been associated with disabling and potentially irreversible serious adverse reactions that can occur together. These include tendinitis and tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, central nervous system effects, and exacerbation of myasthenia gravis. These serious adverse reactions can occur hours to weeks after initiation of therapy. Patients should be advised to discontinue moxifloxacin and contact their physician immediately if they experience symptoms of these reactions. Although systemic absorption with ophthalmic moxifloxacin is generally low, these class warnings are of critical importance and should be considered.

Additionally, serious systemic adverse reactions associated with fluoroquinolones, though less likely with topical ocular administration, include tendinitis and tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, central nervous system effects, exacerbation of myasthenia gravis, QT prolongation, hypersensitivity reactions, risk of aortic aneurysm and dissection, and Clostridioides difficile-associated disease.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions:
Fluoroquinolones, including moxifloxacin, have been associated with disabling and potentially irreversible serious adverse reactions, such as tendinitis and tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, central nervous system effects, and exacerbation of myasthenia gravis. Other serious warnings include QT prolongation, hypersensitivity reactions, and risk of aortic aneurysm and dissection. These systemic warnings should be considered, even with ophthalmic use. Prolonged ophthalmic use may result in the overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms. Patients should avoid wearing contact lenses during treatment.
Specific Considerations: Pregnancy: No definitive data available; consult a doctor. Lactation: Effects are unknown; consult a doctor. Driving: May cause drowsiness; therefore avoid using it while driving (primarily for systemic absorption risk). Liver/Kidney Disease: Consult a doctor for a better analysis if you have liver or kidney disease (primarily for systemic use). clinical_profile.unified_indications: Treatment of various bacterial infections including: acute exacerbation of chronic bronchitis; acute bacterial sinusitis; community acquired pneumonia (especially when other antibiotics cannot be used or have failed); uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections (SSSI); complicated SSSI (including those that have responded to intravenous Moxifloxacin); mild to moderate pelvic inflammatory disease; complicated intra-abdominal infections; and plague.
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Moxifloxacin is a member of the fluoroquinolone class of antibacterial agents.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common side effects include: abdominal pain, bloating, abdominal discomfort, nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, and gastrointestinal upset. More serious adverse reactions, often disabling and potentially irreversible, include: tendinitis and tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, central nervous system effects, QT prolongation (especially in patients with hypokalemia), exacerbation of myasthenia gravis, abnormal liver function tests (LFTs), superinfections, severe skin reactions, and risk of aortic aneurysm and dissection. Clostridioides difficile-associated infection is also a potential adverse reaction.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions:
Patients should complete the entire course of medication to prevent recurrence of infection. 

**Serious and Potentially Irreversible Adverse Reactions**: Moxifloxacin, a fluoroquinolone, is associated with disabling and potentially irreversible serious adverse reactions, including tendinitis, tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, and central nervous system effects. 

**Tendinitis and Tendon Rupture**: Patients are advised to report any limb pain or inflammation immediately, as there is a risk of tendon inflammation or rupture. 

**Peripheral Neuropathy**: May cause damage to nerves resulting in numbness, tingling, or pain. 

**Central Nervous System Effects**: Patients at risk of seizures should discontinue this medication. Other potential effects include headache and dizziness. 

**Exacerbation of Myasthenia Gravis**: Use with caution in patients with myasthenia gravis, as it can worsen muscle weakness. 

**QT Prolongation**: Use with caution, especially in patients with hypokalemia, as it can prolong the QT interval. 

**Pseudomembranous Colitis**: Patients at risk of developing pseudomembranous (antibiotic associated) colitis should stay cautious if they experience persistent diarrhea. 

**Hypersensitivity Reactions**: Severe hypersensitivity reactions are possible. 

**Aortic Aneurysm and Dissection**: Increased risk has been reported. 

**UV Exposure**: Patients are advised to avoid excessive UV exposure. 

**Hepatic and Renal Impairment**: Patients should report signs of hepatic disease or renal impairment. While no dosage adjustment is generally needed for renal or hepatic impairment, caution is advised. 

**Ophthalmological Effects**: Consult an ophthalmologist if any effects on eyes are experienced. 

**Heart Failure**: Use with caution in women and the elderly, particularly concerning heart failure. 

**Storage**: Store at room temperature away from direct heat and sunlight. Keep out of reach of children and pets.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: Moxifloxacin is contraindicated in persons with a history of hypersensitivity to moxifloxacin or any other member of the quinolone class of antibacterials. It is also contraindicated in pregnant females and lactating females.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines:
The recommended oral dose for adults is 400 mg once every 24 hours. The duration of therapy depends on the type of infection:
*   Community Acquired Pneumonia: 7 to 14 days
*   Uncomplicated Skin and Skin Structure Infections (SSSI): 7 days
*   Complicated SSSI: 7 to 21 days
*   Complicated Intra-Abdominal Infections: 5 to 14 days
*   Plague: 10 to 14 days
*   Acute Bacterial Sinusitis: 10 days
*   Acute Bacterial Exacerbation of Chronic Bronchitis: 5 days

No specific dosage adjustment is typically required for patients with renal or hepatic impairment. Patients should complete the entire course of medication as prescribed by their doctor.

clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Not explicitly provided in the available data. Multivitamins work by supplying various essential vitamins and minerals that may be lacking in the diet, thereby supporting various bodily functions and preventing deficiency-related conditions.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common side effects include gastrointestinal disturbances such as constipation, diarrhea, upset stomach, anorexia, or nausea. These are usually mild and may subside with continued use or by taking the supplement with food. Allergic reactions, including sensitizations to folic acid, are possible. A very serious allergic reaction (e.g., severe dizziness, itching, trouble breathing) is rare but requires immediate medical attention. Iron, even at recommended levels, has been associated with gastrointestinal intolerance in some patients.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: Patients should inform their doctor about their complete medical history, especially any known allergies or stomach disturbances, before using this medication. Caution is advised for patients with liver or kidney impairment; consultation with a healthcare professional is recommended before use. Avoid alcohol consumption while taking this medicine. Multivitamins may interact with other medications, including other multivitamins, thyroid medicines, Levodopa, antacids, tetracycline antibiotics, quinolone antibiotics, and anti-seizure drugs; inform your doctor about all concomitant medications. Taking multivitamins containing fat-soluble vitamins on an empty stomach may lead to nausea or reduced absorption; it is generally recommended to take them with food. While multivitamins are generally considered safe during pregnancy and lactation, consultation with a healthcare provider is recommended for more information. This medication doesn’t affect driving ability. Multivitamins do not cause weight gain.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: This product is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to any of its ingredients. All iron compounds are contraindicated in patients with hemosiderosis, hemochromatosis, or hemolytic anemias. Pernicious anemia is a contraindication, as folic acid may obscure its signs and symptoms. Administration to children under 12 years of age is not recommended without specific medical advice, and is contraindicated according to some product specifications.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: For adults (persons over 12 years of age), the typical dosage is one capsule or tablet daily. Take by mouth with a glass of water. It is generally recommended to take multivitamins with food to enhance the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins and minimize potential gastrointestinal discomfort, although specific formulations may suggest taking them between meals. Do not exceed the recommended dosage. For optimal benefit, take this medication regularly. For children, consult a healthcare professional; administration to children under 12 years of age is contraindicated based on some product specifications.

clinical_profile.unified_indications: Used in combination with other immunosuppressants for the prophylaxis of organ rejection in transplant recipients (e.g., kidney, liver, heart).
clinical_profile.unified_mechanism: Mycophenolic acid (MPA), an immunosuppressant, is an uncompetitive and reversible inhibitor of inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase (IMPDH). This inhibits the de novo pathway of guanosine nucleotide synthesis, which is critical for T- and B-lymphocyte proliferation, leading to cytostatic effects on lymphocytes. It has been shown to prevent acute rejection and decrease antibody production.
clinical_profile.unified_side_effects: Common adverse reactions include GI upset (e.g., constipation, nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, dyspepsia, colitis, pancreatitis), infections (e.g., urinary tract infection, CMV infection), hypertension, metabolic disturbances, CNS disturbances (e.g., insomnia), respiratory disorders, anemia, leukopenia, and postoperative pain.
clinical_profile.unified_warnings_and_precautions: **Pregnancy**: This medication is not recommended in pregnant females due to embryo-fetal toxicity risks; refer to boxed warning for details on pregnancy prevention and planning. **Lactation**: Not recommended in lactating females. **Blood Dyscrasias**: Including pure red cell aplasia, anemia, and leukopenia; monitor full blood counts regularly. **Gastrointestinal Complications**: Serious GI tract complications (e.g., colitis, pancreatitis); use with caution in patients with active serious GI disease and in the elderly. **New or Reactivated Viral Infections**: (e.g., CMV, BK virus) can occur. **Acute Inflammatory Syndrome**: Associated with mycophenolate.
clinical_profile.unified_contraindications: History of hypersensitivity, including anaphylaxis, to mycophenolate sodium, mycophenolic acid (MPA), mycophenolate mofetil, or to any of its excipients.
clinical_profile.unified_dosage_guidelines: Adults: 720 mg orally twice daily (1,440 mg total daily dose). Administration: Take on an empty stomach, 1 hour before or 2 hours after food intake. Do not crush, chew, or cut tablets prior to ingestion.
